nodes.statement: The following Lemma \ref{lemma: score_function_norm_bound} follows immediately from Lemmas 20 and 21 in \cite{chen2023improved}.

nodes.name: Score norm bound
assumptions: For any given condition $\mathbf{c}$ and $\tau \in (0, T_g]$
conclusions: \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_\tau(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}\|\nabla\log q_\tau(\mathbf{Y}(\tau) | \mathbf{c})\|^2 \le \frac{d}{\sigma_\tau^2},
nodes.statement: For any given condition $\mathbf{c}$ and $\tau \in (0, T_g]$, and the marginal density $q_\tau(\cdot | \mathbf{c})$ defined by the forward process \eqref{eq: forward_SDE_DDPM}, we have \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_\tau(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}\|\nabla\log q_\tau(\mathbf{Y}(\tau) | \mathbf{c})\|^2 \le \frac{d}{\sigma_\tau^2}, \end{align*} where $\sigma_\tau^2$ is the conditional variance defined in \eqref{eq: forward_SDE_coeff}.
nodes.label: lemma: score_function_norm_bound

nodes.name: Stochastic-localization bound on score difference
assumptions: For any given condition $\mathbf{c}$ and $\tau \in (0, T_g]$
$\tau\in[\tau_{k - 1}, \tau_k]$
conclusions: &\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_\tau(\cdot | \mathbf{c}), \mathbf{Y}(\tau_k)\sim q_{\tau_k | \tau}(\cdot | \mathbf{Y}(\tau), \mathbf{c})}\big[\|\nabla\log q_{\tau}(\mathbf{Y}(\tau) | \mathbf{c}) - \nabla\log q_{\tau_k}(\mathbf{Y}(\tau_k) | \mathbf{c} ) \|^2\big]\\ &\le \int_{\tau}^{\tau_k} f(s)d\sigma^{-2}_{\tau_k} + g^2(s)d\sigma^{-4}_{s} \mathrm{d} s\\ &\qquad + \sigma_{\tau_k}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau_k)\sim q_{\tau_k}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\tau_k}(\mathbf{Y}(\tau_k), \mathbf{c}))] - \sigma_{\tau}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_\tau(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\tau}(\mathbf{Y}(\tau), \mathbf{c}))].
nodes.statement: For any given condition $\mathbf{c}$ and $\tau \in (0, T_g]$, let $q_{0|\tau}(\cdot | \mathbf{y}(\tau), \mathbf{c})$ be the conditional distribution of $\mathbf{Y}(0)$ given $\mathbf{c}$ and $\mathbf{Y}(\tau)=\mathbf{y}(\tau)$, and $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau(\mathbf{y}(\tau), \mathbf{c}) = {\text{Cov}}_{\mathbf{Y}(0)\sim q_{0|\tau}(\cdot | \mathbf{y}(\tau), \mathbf{c})}\big(\mathbf{Y}(0)\big)$ be the corresponding conditional covariance matrix. Then for any $\tau > 0$, when $\tau\in[\tau_{k - 1}, \tau_k]$, we have \begin{align*} &\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_\tau(\cdot | \mathbf{c}), \mathbf{Y}(\tau_k)\sim q_{\tau_k | \tau}(\cdot | \mathbf{Y}(\tau), \mathbf{c})}\big[\|\nabla\log q_{\tau}(\mathbf{Y}(\tau) | \mathbf{c}) - \nabla\log q_{\tau_k}(\mathbf{Y}(\tau_k) | \mathbf{c} ) \|^2\big]\\ &\le \int_{\tau}^{\tau_k} f(s)d\sigma^{-2}_{\tau_k} + g^2(s)d\sigma^{-4}_{s} \mathrm{d} s\\ &\qquad + \sigma_{\tau_k}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau_k)\sim q_{\tau_k}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\tau_k}(\mathbf{Y}(\tau_k), \mathbf{c}))] - \sigma_{\tau}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_\tau(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\tau}(\mathbf{Y}(\tau), \mathbf{c}))]. \end{align*}
nodes.label: lemma: stochastic_char_score_diff

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 8
nodes.statement_short: Bound score differences by Lemmas 9-10 and telescope the posterior-covariance trace terms. The key step rearranges the sum using monotonicity of the trace.
nodes.statement:
For notational simplicity, we introduce  egin{align*} 	au'_{k_0 - 1} = s,\ 	au'_{k} = 	au_k,\ 	ext{for }k=k_0, \cdots, K, \end{align*} which means that $	au_{k}' - 	au_{k - 1}' \le \Delta	au$ for any $k=k_0, \cdots, K$. Now, given the condition $\mathbf{c}$, note that for $\mathbf{Y}(	au)\sim q_	au(\cdot | \mathbf{c})$ and $\mathbf{Y}(	au_k')\sim q_{	au_k' | 	au}(\cdot | \mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{c})$,  egin{align*} & \mathbb{E}_{(\mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{Y}(	au_k'))}  ig[\|g^2(	au)
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) - g^2(	au_k')
abla\log q_{	au_k'}(\mathbf{Y}(	au_k') | \mathbf{c})\|^2 ig]\ &\le 2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)} ig[\|(g^2(	au) - g^2(	au_k'))
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c})\|^2]\ &\qquad + 2\mathbb{E}_{(\mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{Y}(	au_k'))}  ig[g^4(	au_k')\|
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) - 
abla\log q_{	au_k'}(\mathbf{Y}(	au_k') | \mathbf{c})\|^2 ig]\ &\lesssim d(\Delta	au)^2\sigma_	au^{-2} + \mathbb{E}_{(\mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{Y}(	au_k'))}  ig[g^4(	au_k')\|
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) - 
abla\log q_{	au_k'}(\mathbf{Y}(	au_k') | \mathbf{c})\|^2 ig], \end{align*} where the last inequality is from Lemma ef{lemma: score_function_norm_bound}. Then, since $	au_k' = 	au_k$ for $k\ge k_0$, by Lemma ef{lemma: stochastic_char_score_diff} we have  egin{align} & \int_{s}^{	au_{k_0}}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)\sim q_	au(\cdot | \mathbf{c}), \mathbf{Y}(	au_{k_0})\sim q_{	au_{k_0} | 	au}(\cdot | \mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{c})} ig[\|g^2(	au)
abla\log q_{	au}(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) - g^2(	au_{k_0})
abla\log q_{	au_{k_0}}(\mathbf{Y}(	au_{k_0}) | \mathbf{c} ) \|^2 ig] \mathrm{d}	au
onumber\ &\qquad + \sum_{k=k_0 + 1}^{K}\int_{	au_{k - 1}}^{	au_k}\mathbb{E}_{(\mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{Y}(	au_k))} ig[\|g^2(	au)
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) - g^2(	au_k)
abla\log q_{	au_k}(\mathbf{Y}(	au_k) | \mathbf{c})\|^2 ig]\mathrm{d} 	au 
onumber\ &=\sum_{k=k_0}^{K}\int_{	au_{k - 1}'}^{	au_k'}\mathbb{E}_{(\mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{Y}(	au_k'))} ig[\|g^2(	au)
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) - g^2(	au_k')
abla\log q_{	au_k'}(\mathbf{Y}(	au_k') | \mathbf{c})\|^2 ig]\mathrm{d} 	au 
onumber\ & \lesssim \sum_{k=k_0}^{K} \int_{	au_{k -1}'}^{	au_k'}  igg[d(\Delta	au)^2\sigma_	au^{-2} + \int_{	au}^{	au_k'}g^4(	au_k')f(s)d\sigma^{-2}_{	au_k'} + g^4(	au_k')g^2(s)d\sigma^{-4}_{s} \mathrm{d} s  igg]\mathrm{d} 	au \ &\qquad + \sum_{k=k_0}^{K}\int_{	au_{k - 1}'}^{	au_k'} g^4(	au_k') ig(\sigma_{	au_k'}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_k')}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au_k'})] - \sigma_{	au}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au})] ig) \mathrm{d}	au, \end{align} where we omit the dependency of $ oldsymbol{\Sigma}_	au$ on $\mathbf{Y}(	au)$ and $\mathbf{c}$ for simplicity since the context is clear. We first bound \eqref{eq: score_diff_part_1}. Recall that $f(	au) =  rac{1}{2}(a	au + b), g(	au) = \sqrt{a	au + b}$. In addition, $\sigma_	au^{-2}$ is decreasing in $	au$ from \eqref{eq: forward_SDE_coeff} and we have its approximation based on \eqref{eq: expoenetial_approximation}. Then  egin{align} &\sum_{k=k_0}^{K} \int_{	au_{k -1}'}^{	au_k'}  igg[d(\Delta	au)^2\sigma_	au^{-2} + \int_{	au}^{	au_k'}g^4(	au_k')f(s)d\sigma^{-2}_{	au_k'} + g^4(	au_k')g^2(s)d\sigma^{-4}_{s} \mathrm{d} s  igg]\mathrm{d} 	au 
onumber\ &\lesssim \sum_{k=k_0}^{K}\int_{	au_{k - 1}'}^{	au_k'}  igg[d(\Delta	au)^2\sigma_{	au_{k - 1}'}^{-2} + \int_{	au}^{	au_k'} g^4(	au_k')f(	au_k')d\sigma^{-2}_{	au_{k - 1}'} + g^4(	au_k')g^2(	au_k')d\sigma^{-4}_{	au_{k - 1}'} \mathrm{d} s  igg]\mathrm{d} 	au 
onumber\ &\lesssim \sum_{k=k_0}^{k_1}  igg[ rac{d(\Delta	au)^3}{a(	au_{k - 1}')^2/2 + b	au_{k - 1}'}+  rac{d(\Delta	au)^2(a	au_k' + b)^3}{a(	au_{k - 1}')^2/2 + b	au_{k - 1}'} +  rac{d(\Delta	au)^2(a	au_k' + b)^3}{[a(	au_{k - 1}')^2/2 + b	au_{k - 1}']^2} igg] + \sum_{k_1 + 1}^{K} d(\Delta	au)^2(a	au_k' + b)^3
onumber\ &\lesssim d\Delta	au\int_{	au_{k_0 - 1}'}^{	au_{k_1}'}  igg[1 + 	au +  rac{1}{	au} +  rac{1}{	au^2} igg] \mathrm{d}	au + d\Delta	au\int_{	au_{k_1}'}^{T_g} (	au + 1)^3 \mathrm{d}	au
onumber\ &\lesssim d\Delta	au igg[\ln igg( rac{1}{	au_{k_0 - 1}'}  igg) +  rac{1}{	au_{k_0 - 1}'} + (T_g + 1)^4  igg]
onumber\ &= d\Delta	au igg[\ln igg( rac{1}{s}  igg) +  rac{1}{s} + (T_g + 1)^4  igg]. \end{align} We next bound \eqref{eq: score_diff_part_2}. Noting that both $\sigma_	au^2$ and $\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au})]$ are increasing in $	au$ (see \eqref{eq: posterior_cov_trace_dt} and the discussion thereafter), we rearrange the summation to have  egin{align} &\sum_{k=k_0}^{K}\int_{	au_{k - 1}'}^{	au_k'}g^4(	au_k')  ig(\sigma_{	au_k'}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_k')}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au_k}')] - \sigma_{	au}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au})] ig)\mathrm{d}	au 
onumber\ &\le \sum_{k=k_0}^{K}g^4(	au_k')\Delta	au  ig(\sigma_{	au_k'}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_k')}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au_k'})] - \sigma_{	au_k'}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_{k - 1}')}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au_{k - 1}'})] ig)
onumber\ &\lesssim \sum_{k=k_0 - 1}^{k_1} \Delta	au\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_k')}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au_k'})]  ig(g^4(	au_k')\sigma_{	au_k'}^{-4} - g^4(	au_{k + 1}')\sigma_{	au_{k + 1}'}^{-4} ig) 
onumber\ &\qquad + g^4(T_g)\sigma_{	au_{k_1}'}^{-4}\Delta	au \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_{k_1 + 1}')}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au_{k_1 + 1}'})] 
onumber\ &\qquad + g^4(T_g)\sigma_{	au_{k_1}'}^{-4}\Delta	au  igg[\sum_{k=k_1 + 2}^{K} ig(\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_{k}')}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au_{k}'})] - \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_{k - 1}')}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au_{k - 1}'})] ig) igg] 
onumber\ &\overset{\eqref{eq: expoenetial_approximation}}{\lesssim} \Delta	au(T_g + 1)^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(T_g)}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{T_g})] 
onumber\ &\qquad +\sum_{k=k_0 - 1}^{k_1} \Delta	au\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_k')}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au_k'})] igg[ rac{(a	au_k' + b)^2}{[a(	au_k')^2/2 + b	au_k']^{2}} -  rac{(a	au_{k + 1}' + b)^2}{[a(	au_{k + 1}')^2/2 + b	au_{k + 1}']^{2}} igg] 
onumber\ &\lesssim \Delta	au(T_g + 1)^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(T_g)}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{T_g})] + \sum_{k=k_0 - 1}^{k_1} \Delta	au\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_k')}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au_k'})]\cdot igg[ rac{1}{(	au_k')^2} -  rac{1}{(	au_{k + 1}')^2} igg] 
onumber\ &\lesssim \Delta	au(T_g + 1)^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(T_g)}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{T_g})] + \sum_{k=k_0 - 1}^{k_1}  rac{(\Delta	au)^2}{(	au_k')^3}\cdot\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_k')}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au_k'})]. \end{align} Recall that $ oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au} =  oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au}(\mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{c})$ is the conditional variance of $\mathbf{Y}(0)$ given $\mathbf{Y}(	au)$ and $\mathbf{c}$. Then  egin{align} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(T_g)}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{T_g})] \le \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(T_g)} ig[\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(0)|\mathbf{Y}(T_g)}\|\mathbf{Y}(0)\|^2 ig] = \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(0)\sim p_{	ext{target}}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})} ig[\|\mathbf{Y}(0)\|^2 ig]. \end{align} On the other hand, $\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{Y}(0) \sim \mathcal{N} ig(\lambda_	au\mathbf{Y}(0), \sigma_	au^2I_d ig)$ from \eqref{eq: DDPM_conditional_relation}. Then, for $	au < 	au_{k_1}' = 	au_{k_1}$ in \eqref{eq: expoenential_threshold}, using a similar approximation as in \eqref{eq: expoenetial_approximation} we have  egin{align} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au})] &= \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)} ig[	ext{trace} ig({	ext{Cov}}_{\mathbf{Y}(0)|\mathbf{Y}(	au)}[\mathbf{Y}(0)] ig) ig]
onumber\ &=\lambda_{	au}^{-2}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)}  ig[	ext{trace} ig({	ext{Cov}}_{\mathbf{Y}(0)|\mathbf{Y}(	au)}[\lambda_{	au}\mathbf{Y}(0) - \mathbf{Y}(	au)] ig) ig] 
onumber\ &\le \lambda_{	au}^{-2}\mathbb{E}_{(\mathbf{Y}(0), \mathbf{Y}(	au))}  ig[\|\lambda_{	au}\mathbf{Y}(0) - \mathbf{Y}(	au)\|^2 ig] 
onumber\ &= \lambda_	au^{-2}d\sigma_	au^2 = d ig(e^{a	au^2/2 + b	au} - 1 ig)
onumber\ &\asymp d(a	au^2/2 + b	au). \end{align} Substituting \eqref{eq: posterior_trace_bound_1} and \eqref{eq: posterior_trace_bound_2} into \eqref{eq: posterior_trace_diff}, we have  egin{align} &\sum_{k=k_0}^{K}\int_{	au_{k - 1}'}^{	au_k'}g^4(	au_k')  ig(\sigma_{	au_k'}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_k')}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au_k'})] - \sigma_{	au}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au})] ig)\mathrm{d}	au 
onumber\ &\lesssim \Delta	au(T_g + 1)^2 \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(0)} ig[\|\mathbf{Y}(0)\|^2 ig] + \sum_{k=k_0 - 1}^{k_1}  rac{(\Delta	au)^2d[a(	au_k')^2/2 + b	au_k' ]}{(	au_k')^3} 
onumber \ &\lesssim \Delta	au(T_g + 1)^2 \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(0)} ig[\|\mathbf{Y}(0)\|^2 ig] + d\Delta	au \int_{	au_{k_0 - 1}'}^{	au_{k_1}'} igg[ rac{1}{	au} +  rac{1}{	au^2} igg] \mathrm{d}	au 
onumber\ &\lesssim \Delta	au(T_g + 1)^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(0)} ig[\|\mathbf{Y}(0)\|^2 ig] + d\Delta	au igg[\ln igg( rac{1}{	au_{k_0 - 1}'}  igg) +  rac{1}{	au_{k_0 - 1}'} igg]
onumber\ &= \Delta	au(T_g + 1)^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(0)\sim p_{	ext{target}}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})} ig[\|\mathbf{Y}(0)\|^2 ig] + d\Delta	au igg[\ln igg( rac{1}{s}  igg) +  rac{1}{s} igg]. \end{align} The proof is complete by combining \eqref{eq: score_diff_bound_1} and \eqref{eq: score_diff_bound_2}.

abla\log q_{	au}(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) - g^2(	au_{k_0})

&\sum_{k=k_0}^{K}\int_{	au_{k - 1}'}^{	au_k'}g^4(	au_k')  ig(\sigma_{	au_k'}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_k')}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au_k}')] - \sigma_{	au}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au})] ig)\mathrm{d}	au

onumber\ &\qquad +\sum_{k=k_0 - 1}^{k_1} \Delta	au\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_k')}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au_k'})] igg[ rac{(a	au_k' + b)^2}{[a(	au_k')^2/2 + b	au_k']^{2}} -  rac{(a	au_{k + 1}' + b)^2}{[a(	au_{k + 1}')^2/2 + b	au_{k + 1}']^{2}} igg]

nodes.name: Hessian of log-density bound
assumptions: For any given condition $\mathbf{c}$ and any $\tau \in (0, T_g]$
conclusions: \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_\tau(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}\big[\|\nabla^2\log q_\tau(\mathbf{Y}_\tau|\mathbf{c})\|_F^2\big]\le d\sigma_\tau^{-4} + \frac{1}{g^2(\tau)}\cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\tau}\bigg(\sigma_\tau^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_\tau(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau(\mathbf{Y}(\tau), \mathbf{c}))]\bigg).
nodes.statement: For any given condition $\mathbf{c}$ and any $\tau \in (0, T_g]$, we have \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_\tau(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}\big[\|\nabla^2\log q_\tau(\mathbf{Y}_\tau|\mathbf{c})\|_F^2\big]\le d\sigma_\tau^{-4} + \frac{1}{g^2(\tau)}\cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\tau}\bigg(\sigma_\tau^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_\tau(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau(\mathbf{Y}(\tau), \mathbf{c}))]\bigg). \end{align*}
nodes.label: lemma: hessian_score_bound

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 10
nodes.statement_short: Derive the SDE of the score along the reverse process via Ito and Fokker-Planck, then use Ito isometry with Lemma 11. Integrating the resulting derivative bound over a step gives the result.
nodes.statement:
Following \cite{bentonnearly}, we first consider the stochastic dynamic of the score function $ ig\{
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ): 	au\in[0, T_g) ig\}$ under a given condition $\mathbf{c}$. Recall that the reverse SDE \eqref{eq: reverse_SDE_DDPM} of diffusion models is  egin{align*} \mathrm{d}	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) = [	ilde f(	au)	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) + 	ilde g^2(	au) 
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde {\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c})]\mathrm{d}	au + 	ilde g(	au) \mathrm{d}	ilde{\mathbf{B}}(	au), \end{align*} where $	ilde f(	au) := f(T_g - 	au)$ and $	ilde g(	au) := g(T_g - 	au)$. As in the proof of Lemma 3 of \cite{bentonnearly}, $
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})$ is smooth for $	au\in[0, T_g)$, and by It\^{o}'s formula we can write  egin{align} \mathrm{d} ig[
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) ig] &=  igg\{
abla^2\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} )\cdot ig[	ilde f(	au)	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) + 	ilde g^2(	au) 
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde {\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) ig]
onumber\ &\qquad \quad +  rac{1}{2}	ilde g^2(	au)\cdot \Delta  ig(
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) ig) igg\}\mathrm{d}	au +  rac{\mathrm{d} ig[
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) ig]}{\mathrm{d} 	au} \mathrm{d} 	au 
onumber\ &\qquad + 	ilde g(	au)
abla^2\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) \mathrm{d}	ilde{\mathbf{B}}(	au). \end{align} To further simplify \eqref{eq: score_function_ito}, consider the Fokker–Planck equation for the forward process \eqref{eq: forward_SDE_DDPM}:  egin{align*} \mathrm{d} q_	au(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c}) =  igg(-
abla\cdot ig[(-f(	au)q_	au(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c})\mathbf{y}  ig] +  rac{1}{2}\Delta ig[g^2(	au)q_	au(\mathbf{y}|\mathbf{c}) ig] igg)\mathrm{d}	au, \end{align*} leading to  egin{align*} \mathrm{d}(\log q_	au(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c})) &=  rac{1}{q_	au(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c})} igg(-
abla\cdot ig[(-f(	au) q_	au(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c})\mathbf{y} ig] +  rac{1}{2} \Delta ig[g^2(	au)q_	au(\mathbf{y}|\mathbf{c}) ig] igg)\mathrm{d}	au\ &=  igg(f(	au)d + f(	au)\mathbf{y}^T
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c}) +  rac{1}{2}g^2(	au)\Delta\log q_	au(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c}) +  rac{1}{2}g^2(	au)\|
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c})\|^2 igg)\mathrm{d} 	au. \end{align*} It follows that  egin{equation}  egin{split} & rac{\mathrm{d} ig[
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c} ) ig]}{\mathrm{d} 	au} = 
abla rac{\mathrm{d}(\log q_{T_g - 	au}(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c}))}{\mathrm{d} 	au} \ &= - igg(	ilde f(	au)
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c}) + 	ilde f(	au)
abla^2\log q_{T_g - 	au}(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c})\cdot\mathbf{y} \ & \quad \qquad +  rac{1}{2}	ilde g^2(	au)
abla ig(\Delta\log q_{T_g - 	au}(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c}) ig) + 	ilde g^2(	au)
abla^2\log q_{T_g - 	au}(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c})\cdot 
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c}) igg). \end{split} \end{equation} Substituting \eqref{eq: score_function_time_derivative} into \eqref{eq: score_function_ito} and simplifying, we obtain  egin{align} \mathrm{d} ig[
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) ig] = -	ilde f(	au)
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) \mathrm{d} 	au + 	ilde g(	au)
abla^2\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) \mathrm{d}	ilde{\mathbf{B}}(	au). \end{align} Now, we establish the desired bound. First, for fixed $s \in (0, 	au)$, we have  egin{align*} &\mathrm{d} ig[(
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} ))^T
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) ig] \ &= -	ilde f(	au)(
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} ))^T
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) \mathrm{d} 	au \ &\qquad + 	ilde g(	au)(
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} ))^T
abla^2\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) \mathrm{d}	ilde{\mathbf{B}}(	au). \end{align*} By Lemma ef{lemma: hessian_score_bound}, $\int_{s}^	au \mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(u)} ig[\|
abla^2\log q_{T_g - u}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(u))\|^2_F ig]\mathrm{d} u < \infty$ where $	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(u)\sim q_{T_g - u}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})$, implying that the final term in the above equation is a square-integrable martingale. Integrating on both sides and taking expectations w.r.t. the joint distribution of $(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s))$ induced by \eqref{eq: reverse_SDE_DDPM}, we get  egin{equation}  egin{split} & rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}	au}\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s))} ig[(
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} ))^T
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) ig]\ &= -\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s))} ig[	ilde f(	au)(
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} ))^T
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c})  ig]. \end{split} \end{equation} Next, if setting $	ilde\Lambda(	au) = \exp ig(\int_0^	au 	ilde f(s)\mathrm{d} s  ig)$ and applying It\^{o}'s formula to \eqref{eq: score_function_process}, we obtain  egin{align*} \mathrm{d} ig[	ilde\Lambda(	au)
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) ig] = 	ilde\Lambda(	au)	ilde g(	au)
abla^2\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) \mathrm{d}	ilde{\mathbf{B}}(	au). \end{align*} We know from Lemma ef{lemma: hessian_score_bound} that $\int_{s}^	au	ilde\Lambda^2(u)\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(u)}  ig[\|
abla^2\log q_{T_g - u}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(u))\|^2_F ig]\mathrm{d} u < \infty$ for any fixed $s > 0$. By It\^{o}'s isometry and chain rule, we obtain  egin{align*} &	ilde\Lambda^2(	au)	ilde g^2(	au)\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)} ig[\|
abla^2\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c})\|^2_F ig]\ &=  rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}	au}\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s))} ig[\|	ilde\Lambda(	au)
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) - 	ilde\Lambda(s)
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} )\|^2 ig] 
onumber\ &= 	ilde\Lambda^2(	au)\cdot  rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}	au}\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)} ig[\|

abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) ||^2\ &\qquad - 2	ilde\Lambda(	au)	ilde\Lambda(s)\cdot  rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}	au}\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s))} ig[(

abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ))^T
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} ) ig]\ &\overset{\eqref{eq: score_process_corss_term_dt}}{=} 	ilde\Lambda^2(	au)\cdot  rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}	au}\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)} ig[\|

abla^2\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c})\|^2_F ig]. \end{split} \end{equation} For any fixed $s > 0$ and $	au > s$, \eqref{eq: score_process_corss_term_dt} and \eqref{eq: F_norm_characterization} lead to  egin{align*} & rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}	au}\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s))}  ig[\|
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) - 
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} )\|^2 ig]\ &=  rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}	au}\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)} ig[\|
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} )\|^2 ig] - 2 rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}	au}\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s))} ig[(
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ))^T
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} ) ig]\ &= 	ilde g^2(	au)\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)} ig[\|
abla^2\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c})\|^2_F ig] - 2	ilde f(	au)\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)} ig[\|
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) ||^2\ &\qquad + 2\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s))} ig[	ilde f(	au)(
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} ))^T
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c})  ig]\ &= 	ilde g^2(	au)\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)} ig[\|
abla^2\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c})\|^2_F ig] \ &\qquad - 2	ilde f(	au)\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s))} ig[\|
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) - 
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} )||^2 ig]\ &\qquad + 2	ilde f(	au)\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s))}  ig[(
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} ) - 
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ))^T
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} ) ig]. \end{align*} However, by Young's inequality,  egin{align*} &\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s))} ig[(
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) -

abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} ) ig]\ &\le  rac{1}{2} igg[\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s))} ig[\|
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) - 
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} )\|^2 ig] + \mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s)} ig[\|
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} )\|^2 ig] igg]. \end{align*} Therefore, we have  egin{align*} & rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}	au}\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s))}  ig[\|
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) - 
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} )\|^2 ig]\ &\le 	ilde f(	au)\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s)} ig[\|
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} )\|^2 ig] + 	ilde g^2(	au)\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)} ig[\|
abla^2\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c})\|^2_F ig]. \end{align*} Let $s=	au_k$ and $	au\in[	au_k, 	au_{k + 1}]$. Integrate both sides of the above equation from $	au_k$ to $	au$ and use Lemma ef{lemma: score_function_norm_bound} and Lemma ef{lemma: hessian_score_bound} to obtain  egin{align*} &\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au_k))} ig[\|
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) - 
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au_k}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au_k) | \mathbf{c} )\|^2 ig]\ &\le \int_{	au_k}^{	au}	ilde f(u)\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au_k)} ig[\|
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au_k}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au_k) | \mathbf{c} )\|^2 ig] + 	ilde g^2(u)\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(u)} ig[\|
abla^2\log q_{T_g - u}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(u) | \mathbf{c})\|^2_F ig]\mathrm{d} u\ &\le \int_{	au_k}^{	au}	ilde f(u)d\sigma^{-2}_{T_g - 	au_k} + 	ilde g^2(u)d\sigma^{-4}_{T_g - u} -  rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} r} ig(\sigma_{T - r}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(r)\sim q_{T_g - r}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{T_g - r})] ig) ig|_{r=u} \mathrm{d} u\ &\le \int_{	au_k}^{	au}	ilde f(u)d\sigma^{-2}_{T_g - 	au_k} + 	ilde g^2(u)d\sigma^{-4}_{T_g - u} \mathrm{d} u \ &\qquad + \sigma_{T - 	au_k}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(T_g - 	au_k)}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{T_g - 	au_k})] - \sigma_{T - 	au}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(T_g - 	au)}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{T_g - 	au})], \end{align*} where we omit to write out the dependency of $ oldsymbol{\Sigma}_	au$ on $\mathbf{Y}(	au)$ and $\mathbf{c}$ for simplicity. Finally, for the forward process $\mathbf{Y}$ in \eqref{eq: forward_SDE_DDPM}, since $	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) = \mathbf{Y}(T_g - 	au)$ for any $	au\in[0, T_g]$, we have for $	au >0$ and $	au\in[	au_{k - 1}, 	au_k]$,  egin{align*} &\mathbb{E}_{(\mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{Y}(	au_k))} ig[\|
abla\log q_{	au}(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) - 
abla\log q_{	au_k}(\mathbf{Y}(	au_k) | \mathbf{c} ) \|^2 ig]\ &\le \int_{	au}^{	au_k} f(s)d\sigma^{-2}_{	au_k} + g^2(s)d\sigma^{-4}_{s} \mathrm{d} s +  ig(\sigma_{	au_k}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_k)}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au_k})] - \sigma_{	au}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au})] ig). \end{align*} This completes our proof.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5
nodes.statement_short: Bound the score norm separately below and above the Lipschitz threshold and integrate.
nodes.statement:
For a given condition $\mathbf{c}$, recall the definition of $	au_{lipz}(\mathbf{c}), k_0(\mathbf{c})$ and $k_1$ in the proof of Lemma ef{lemma: score_discretization_error_bound} in Appendix ef{sec: score_discretization_error}. By Lemma 14 and Lemma 21 of \cite{chen2023improved} and our Lemma ef{lemma: score_function_norm_bound}, we can derive  egin{align*} &\sum_{k=1}^{K}\int_{	au_{k - 1}}^{	au_{k}}[g^2(	au_k) - g^2(	au)]^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)\sim q_{	au}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}  ig[ ig\|
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) ig\|^2 ig] \mathrm{d}	au\ &\lesssim \sum_{k=1}^{K}\int_{	au_{k - 1}}^{	au_{k}}(\Delta	au)^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)\sim q_{	au}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}  ig[ ig\|
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) ig\|^2 ig] \mathrm{d}	au\ &\lesssim \sum_{k=1}^{k_0(\mathbf{c}) - 1}  igg[\int_{	au_{k - 1}}^{	au_{k}}(\Delta	au)^2\cdot dL(\mathbf{c})\lambda_	au^{-1} \mathrm{d}	au  igg] + \int_{	au_{k_0(\mathbf{c}) - 1}}^{	au_{lipz}(\mathbf{c})}(\Delta	au)^2\cdot dL(\mathbf{c})\lambda_	au^{-1} \mathrm{d}	au \ &\qquad + \int_{	au_{lipz}(\mathbf{c})}^{	au_{k_0(\mathbf{c})}}(\Delta	au)^2\cdot d\sigma^{-2}_	au \mathrm{d}	au + \sum_{k_0(\mathbf{c}) + 1}^K igg[\int_{	au_{k - 1}}^{	au_{k}}(\Delta	au)^2\cdot d\sigma^{-2}_	au \mathrm{d}	au igg]\ &\overset{\eqref{eq: expoenetial_approximation} }{\lesssim} \int_{0}^{	au_{lipz}(\mathbf{c})} d(\Delta	au)^2L(\mathbf{c})(1 + a	au^2/4 + b	au/2) \mathrm{d}	au + \int_{	au_{lipz}(\mathbf{c})}^{	au_{k_1}}  rac{d(\Delta	au)^2}{a	au^2/2 + b	au} \mathrm{d}	au + \int_{	au_{k_1}}^{T_g} d(\Delta	au)^2 \mathrm{d}	au\ &\lesssim d(\Delta	au)^2L(\mathbf{c})\cdot 	au_{lipz}(\mathbf{c}) + d(\Delta	au)^2\int_{	au_{lipz}(\mathbf{c})}^{	au_{k_1}} igg( rac{1}{	au} +  rac{1}{	au^2}  igg)\mathrm{d}	au + d(\Delta	au)^2T_g\ &\overset{\eqref{eq: lipz_index_approximation}}{\lesssim} d(\Delta	au)^2 igg(L(\mathbf{c}) + 2L_2(\mathbf{c}) + 1/2 + \ln ig(2L_2(\mathbf{c}) + 1/2 ig) + T_g  igg)\ &\overset{\eqref{eq: lipschitz_constant}}{\lesssim} d(\Delta	au)^2 igg(L(\mathbf{c}) + T_g + 1  igg). \end{align*} Taking expectation on both sides w.r.t. $\mathbf{c}\sim\mathbf{C}$, we obtain  egin{align*} &\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{c}\sim\mathbf{C}} igg[\sum_{k=1}^{K}\int_{	au_{k - 1}}^{	au_{k}}[g^2(	au_k) - g^2(	au)]^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)\sim q_{	au}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}  ig[ ig\|
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) ig\|^2 ig] \mathrm{d}	au igg]\ &\lesssim d(\Delta	au)^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{c}\sim\mathbf{C}} igg[L(\mathbf{c}) + T_g + 1 igg]\ &\lesssim d(\Delta	au)^2[L_1 + T_g + 1]. \end{align*} The proof is therefore complete.

onumber\ &\qquad +  rac{1}{2} igg[ rac{C_{	ext{KL}}}{2}- 	ilde g^2(	au_k) igg] \mathbb{E}_{ ar{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) \sim  ar p_	au} igg\|
abla\log rac{ ar p_	au( ar{\mathbf{Y}}(	au))}{ ar p_	au^	heta( ar{\mathbf{Y}}(	au))} igg\|^2,

nodes.name: Stochastic localization process
nodes.statement: Give a random variable $\xi\sim p_{\text{target}}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})$, the stochastic localization considers a process $\big(\mathbf{U}(s)\big)_{s\ge0}$ defined by \begin{align} \mathbf{U}(s) = s\xi + \bar{\mathbf{B}}(s),\ \text{for } s \ge 0, \end{align} where $\bar{\mathbf{B}}$ is a $d$-dimensional standard Brownian motion independent of $\xi$.
nodes.section: C.2 Proof of Lemma 11 via Stochastic Localization

nodes.name: Eq. (57): stochastic localization
nodes.statement: \mathbf{U}(s) = s\xi + \bar{\mathbf{B}}(s),\ \text{for } s \ge 0,
nodes.section: C.2 Proof of Lemma 11 via Stochastic Localization
nodes.label: eq: stochastic_localization

nodes.name: Posterior covariance $\mathbf{A}_s$
nodes.statement: Denote the posterior covariance of $\xi$ given $\mathbf{U}(s)$ and $\mathbf{c}$ by $\mathbf{A}_s(\mathbf{U}(s), \mathbf{c}) = {\text{Cov}}_{\xi|(\mathbf{U}(s), \mathbf{c})}(\xi)$.
nodes.section: C.2 Proof of Lemma 11 via Stochastic Localization

nodes.name: Posterior covariance dynamics under stochastic localization
conclusions: \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} s}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{U}(s)}\big[\mathbf{A}_s\big] = -\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{U}(s)}\big[\mathbf{A}_s^2\big],\quad \text{for } s\ge 0,
nodes.statement: Then, we have the following characterization {\cite[Proposition 2]{bentonnearly}}: \begin{equation} \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} s}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{U}(s)}\big[\mathbf{A}_s\big] = -\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{U}(s)}\big[\mathbf{A}_s^2\big],\quad \text{for } s\ge 0, \end{equation} where the expectation is taken w.r.t. the marginal distribution of $\mathbf{U}(s)$ given $\mathbf{c}$, and we omit the dependence of $\mathbf{A}_s$ on $\mathbf{U}(s)$ and $\mathbf{c}$ for notational simplicity.
nodes.section: C.2 Proof of Lemma 11 via Stochastic Localization

nodes.name: Eq. (58): stochastic posterior cov dt
nodes.statement: \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} s}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{U}(s)}\big[\mathbf{A}_s\big] = -\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{U}(s)}\big[\mathbf{A}_s^2\big],\quad \text{for } s\ge 0,
nodes.section: C.2 Proof of Lemma 11 via Stochastic Localization
nodes.label: eq: stochastic_posterior_cov_dt

nodes.name: Forward OU process as time-changed stochastic localization
assumptions: Under condition $\mathbf{c}$, if we define the process $\mathbf{Y}$ and $\mathbf{U}$ according to \eqref{eq: forward_SDE_DDPM} and \eqref{eq: stochastic_localization}, respectively
conclusions: $\{\mathbf{U}(s): s\ge 0\}$ and $\{ s\lambda_{\tau(s)}^{-1}\mathbf{Y}(\tau(s)): s\ge 0\}$ have the same law
nodes.statement: Under condition $\mathbf{c}$, if we define the process $\mathbf{Y}$ and $\mathbf{U}$ according to \eqref{eq: forward_SDE_DDPM} and \eqref{eq: stochastic_localization}, respectively, and consider a time change \begin{equation} \tau(s) = \inf\big\{u: \exp(au^2/2 + bu) - 1 > s^{-1}\big\}, \end{equation} then $\{\mathbf{U}(s): s\ge 0\}$ and $\{ s\lambda_{\tau(s)}^{-1}\mathbf{Y}(\tau(s)): s\ge 0\}$ have the same law, where $\lambda_\tau$ is defined in \eqref{eq: forward_SDE_coeff}.
nodes.section: C.2 Proof of Lemma 11 via Stochastic Localization
nodes.label: lemma: diffusion_time_change

nodes.name: Eq. (59): diffusion localization time change
nodes.statement: \tau(s) = \inf\big\{u: \exp(au^2/2 + bu) - 1 > s^{-1}\big\},
nodes.section: C.2 Proof of Lemma 11 via Stochastic Localization
nodes.label: eq: diffusion_localization_time_change

nodes.name: Posterior distribution $q_{0|\tau}$
nodes.statement: Denote by $q_{0|\tau}(\cdot | \mathbf{y}(\tau), \mathbf{c})$ the posterior distribution of $\mathbf{Y}(0)$ given $\mathbf{c}$ and $\mathbf{Y}(\tau)=\mathbf{y}(\tau)$.
nodes.section: C.2 Proof of Lemma 11 via Stochastic Localization

nodes.name: Posterior covariance $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau$
nodes.statement: Let the posterior covariance matrix be $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau(\mathbf{y}(\tau), \mathbf{c}) := {\text{Cov}}_{\mathbf{Y}(0)\sim q_{0|\tau}(\cdot | \mathbf{y}(\tau), \mathbf{c})}\big[\mathbf{Y}(0)\big]$, for which we may omit its dependence on $\mathbf{y}(\tau)$ and $\mathbf{c}$ when the context is clear.
nodes.section: C.2 Proof of Lemma 11 via Stochastic Localization

nodes.name: Posterior covariance moments coincide under the time change
nodes.statement_short: Under the time change of Lemma 12 the first two moments of $\Sigma_\tau$ equal those of the localization covariance $A_s$.
nodes.statement: Then, for any $s > 0$, when $\tau = \tau(s)$, it follows from Lemma \ref{lemma: diffusion_time_change} that \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}\big[\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\tau}^2\big] &= \int_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^d} [{\text{Cov}}(\mathbf{Y}(0) | \mathbf{Y}(\tau) = \mathbf{y}, \mathbf{c})]^2 \mathrm{d} P_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}(\mathbf{y})\\ &= \int_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^d} [{\text{Cov}}(\mathbf{Y}(0) | s\lambda_\tau^{-1}\mathbf{Y}(\tau) = s\lambda_\tau^{-1}\mathbf{y}, \mathbf{c})]^2 \mathrm{d} P_{s\lambda_\tau^{-1}\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}(s\lambda_\tau^{-1}\mathbf{y})\\ & = \int_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^d} [{\text{Cov}}(\xi | \mathbf{U}(s) = s\lambda_\tau^{-1}\mathbf{y}, \mathbf{c})]^2 \mathrm{d} P_{\mathbf{U}(s)}(s\lambda_\tau^{-1}\mathbf{y})\\ &=\int_{\mathbf{u}\in\mathbb{R}^d} [{\text{Cov}}(\xi | \mathbf{U}(s) = \mathbf{u}, \mathbf{c})]^2 \mathrm{d} P_{\mathbf{U}(s)}(\mathbf{u})\\ &= \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{U}(s)}\big[\mathbf{A}_s^2\big], \end{align*} and similarly $\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{U}(s)}\big[\mathbf{A}_s\big] = \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}\big[\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\tau}\big]$, where the expectations involving $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\tau} = \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\tau}(\mathbf{Y}(\tau), \mathbf{c})$ are taken w.r.t. $\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_\tau(\cdot | \mathbf{c})$ of the forward process \eqref{eq: forward_SDE_DDPM}, and $P_{\mathbf{M}}$ is the distribution function of a general random variable $\mathbf{M}$.
nodes.section: C.2 Proof of Lemma 11 via Stochastic Localization

nodes.name: Time derivative of posterior covariance
nodes.statement: Equation \eqref{eq: stochastic_posterior_cov_dt} yields \begin{align} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}\big[\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\tau}^2\big] = \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{U}(s)}\big[\mathbf{A}_s^2\big] = -\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} s}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{U}(s)}\big[\mathbf{A}_s\big] = -\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} s}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau(s))}\big[\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\tau(s)}\big] = -\frac{\mathrm{d} \tau(s)}{\mathrm{d} s}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} \tau}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}\big[\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\tau}\big]. \end{align}
nodes.section: C.2 Proof of Lemma 11 via Stochastic Localization

nodes.name: Eq. (60): posterior cov dt
nodes.statement: \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}\big[\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\tau}^2\big] = \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{U}(s)}\big[\mathbf{A}_s^2\big] = -\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} s}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{U}(s)}\big[\mathbf{A}_s\big] = -\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} s}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau(s))}\big[\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\tau(s)}\big] = -\frac{\mathrm{d} \tau(s)}{\mathrm{d} s}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} \tau}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}\big[\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\tau}\big].
nodes.section: C.2 Proof of Lemma 11 via Stochastic Localization
nodes.label: eq: posterior_cov_dt

nodes.name: Trace derivative identity and monotonicity of posterior covariance trace
conclusions: $\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}\big[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\tau})\big]$ is increasing in $\tau$
nodes.statement_short: Relates $E[\mathrm{tr}\Sigma_\tau^2]$ to the derivative of $E[\mathrm{tr}\Sigma_\tau]$, which is therefore increasing in $\tau$.
nodes.statement: Note that $\sigma_\tau^2 = 1 - \exp(-a\tau^2/2 - b\tau)$, and $\frac{\mathrm{d}(\sigma_\tau^2)}{\mathrm{d} \tau} = 2\sigma_\tau \frac{\mathrm{d} \sigma_\tau}{\mathrm{d} \tau} := 2\sigma_\tau\dot{\sigma}_\tau = (a\tau + b)\exp(-a\tau^2/2 - b\tau)$. Hence, for $\tau = \tau(s)$, \begin{align*} s^{-1} = \exp(a\tau^2/2 + b\tau) - 1 = \frac{1}{1 - \sigma_\tau^2} - 1 = \frac{\sigma_\tau^2}{1 - \sigma_\tau^2}, \end{align*} which indicates that $\frac{\mathrm{d} s}{\mathrm{d} \tau} = \big[-2\dot\sigma_\tau\sigma_\tau\cdot \sigma_\tau^2 - 2\dot\sigma_\tau\sigma_\tau(1 - \sigma_\tau^2)\big]/\sigma_\tau^4 = -2\dot\sigma_\tau/\sigma_\tau^3$. Then, by taking the trace of both sides of \eqref{eq: posterior_cov_dt}, we obtain \begin{align} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}\big[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau^2)\big] = -\frac{\mathrm{d} \tau(s)}{\mathrm{d} s}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} \tau}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}\big[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\tau})\big] = \frac{\sigma_\tau^3}{2\dot\sigma_\tau}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} \tau}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}\big[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\tau})\big], \end{align} which also implies that $\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}\big[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\tau})\big]$ is increasing in $\tau$ since $\sigma_\tau\dot\sigma_\tau \ge 0$ for all $\tau\ge 0$.
nodes.section: C.2 Proof of Lemma 11 via Stochastic Localization

nodes.name: Eq. (61): posterior cov trace dt
nodes.statement: \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}\big[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau^2)\big] = -\frac{\mathrm{d} \tau(s)}{\mathrm{d} s}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} \tau}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}\big[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\tau})\big] = \frac{\sigma_\tau^3}{2\dot\sigma_\tau}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} \tau}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}\big[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\tau})\big],
nodes.section: C.2 Proof of Lemma 11 via Stochastic Localization
nodes.label: eq: posterior_cov_trace_dt

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 11
nodes.statement_short: Express the Hessian of $\log q_\tau$ via the posterior covariance and use the trace identity (61).
nodes.statement: Recall that $\mathbf{Y}(\tau) | \mathbf{Y}(0)\sim\mathcal{N}(\lambda_\tau\mathbf{Y}(0), \sigma_\tau^2I_d)$. Using a similar argument as in the proof of Lemma 5 of \cite{bentonnearly}, we obtain \begin{align*} \nabla^2\log q_\tau(\mathbf{y}_\tau|\mathbf{c}) = -\sigma_\tau^{-2}I_d + \sigma_\tau^{-4}{\text{Cov}}_{q_{0|\tau}(\cdot | \mathbf{y}(\tau), \mathbf{c})}\big(\mathbf{y}(\tau) - \lambda_\tau\mathbf{Y}(0)\big) = -\sigma_\tau^{-2}I_d + \sigma_\tau^{-4}\lambda_\tau^2\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau. \end{align*} Noting that $\|A\|_F^2 = \text{trace}(A^TA)$ for a matrix $A$ and that $1 > \lambda_\tau^2 = \exp(-a\tau^2/2 - b\tau) = 2\sigma_\tau\dot\sigma_\tau/(a\tau + b)$, we can directly compute \begin{align*} &\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_\tau(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}\big[\|\nabla^2\log q_\tau(\mathbf{Y}_\tau|\mathbf{c})\|_F^2\big] \\ &= d\sigma_\tau^{-4} - 2\sigma_\tau^{-6}\lambda_\tau^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau)] + \sigma_\tau^{-8}\lambda_\tau^4\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau^2)]\\ &\le d\sigma_\tau^{-4} - 2\sigma_\tau^{-6}\lambda_\tau^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau)] + \sigma_\tau^{-8}\lambda_\tau^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau^2)]\\ &\overset{\eqref{eq: posterior_cov_trace_dt}}{=} d\sigma_\tau^{-4} - \frac{4\sigma_\tau^{-5}\dot\sigma_\tau}{a\tau + b}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau)] + \frac{2\sigma_\tau^{-7}\dot\sigma_\tau}{a\tau + b}\cdot \frac{\sigma_\tau^3}{2\dot\sigma_\tau}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\tau}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau)]\\ &= d\sigma_\tau^{-4} - \frac{4\sigma_\tau^{-5}\dot\sigma_\tau}{a\tau + b}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau)] + \frac{\sigma_\tau^{-4}}{a\tau + b}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\tau}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau))}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau)]\\ &= d\sigma_\tau^{-4} + \frac{1}{a\tau + b}\cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\tau}\bigg(\sigma_\tau^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_\tau(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau)]\bigg). \end{align*} The proof is complete by virtue of $g^2(\tau) = a\tau + b$.
nodes.section: C.2 Proof of Lemma 11 via Stochastic Localization

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 12
nodes.statement_short: Apply Ito's formula and the Dambis-Dubins-Schwarz time change to rewrite the scaled forward process as a stochastic localization.
nodes.statement: Letting $\Lambda(\tau) = \exp\big(\int_{0}^\tau f(s)\mathrm{d} s\big)$ and applying It\^{o}'s formula to the forward SDE \eqref{eq: forward_SDE_DDPM} under the condition $\mathbf{c}$, we have \begin{align*} \mathrm{d} [\Lambda(\tau)\mathbf{Y}(\tau)] = f(\tau)\Lambda(\tau)\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau + \Lambda(\tau)\big[-f(\tau)\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau + g(\tau)\mathrm{d} \mathbf{B}(\tau)\big] = \Lambda(\tau)g(\tau)\mathrm{d} \mathbf{B}(\tau). \end{align*} By the Dambis-Dubins–Schwarz theorem {\citep[Theorem 3.4.6]{karatzas2014brownian}}, there is a process $(\hat{\mathbf{B}}(s))_{s\ge 0}$ such that under the time change \begin{align*} \kappa(s) := \inf\bigg\{\tau: \int_{0}^\tau\Lambda^2(u)g^2(u)\mathrm{d} u > s\bigg\} = \inf\bigg\{\tau: \exp\big(a\tau^2/2 + b\tau\big) - 1> s\bigg\}, \end{align*} we have \begin{align*} \hat{\mathbf{B}}(e^{a\tau^2/2 + b\tau} - 1) = \int_{0}^\tau\Lambda(u)g(u)\mathrm{d} \mathbf{B}(u), \end{align*} where $(\hat{\mathbf{B}}(s))_{s\ge 0}$ is a standard Brownian motion w.r.t. the filtration $\big(\mathcal{F}_{\kappa(s)}\big)_{s\ge0}$, while $(\mathcal{F}_\tau)_{\tau \ge 0}$ is the natural filtration generated by $(\mathbf{B}(\tau))_{\tau \ge 0}$. Then, for any $s > 0$, we have \begin{align*} \Lambda(\kappa(s))\mathbf{Y}(\kappa(s)) = \mathbf{Y}(0) + \int_{0}^{\kappa(s)}\Lambda(u)g(u)\mathrm{d} \mathbf{B}(u) = \mathbf{Y}(0) + \hat{\mathbf{B}}(s). \end{align*} Now, if we set $\mathbf{U}(0) = 0$ and \begin{align*} \mathbf{U}(s) := s\Lambda(\kappa(s^{-1}))\mathbf{Y}(\kappa(s^{-1})) = s\mathbf{Y}(0) + s\hat{\mathbf{B}}(s^{-1}),\ \text{for } s > 0, \end{align*} then we find that $\mathbf{U}$ satisfies the definition of the stochastic localization in \eqref{eq: stochastic_localization}, because $\mathbf{Y}(0)\sim p_{\text{target}}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})$ and the law of $\big(s\hat{\mathbf{B}}(s^{-1})\big)_{s\ge 0}$ is the same as the law of $\big(\hat{\mathbf{B}}(s)\big)_{s\ge 0}$. The proof is complete by noting that $\kappa(s^{-1}) = \tau(s)$ in \eqref{eq: diffusion_localization_time_change} and $\Lambda(\tau) = \lambda_\tau^{-1}$ in \eqref{eq: forward_SDE_coeff}.
nodes.section: C.2 Proof of Lemma 11 via Stochastic Localization

nodes.name: Offline q-learning mean-variance algorithm with synthetic wealth simulator
input: number of real asset price paths $H$
number of synthetic paths (generated at each episode) $H_s$
nodes.statement_short: Actor-critic q-learning for continuous-time mean-variance portfolio selection, training on real plus generated synthetic price paths.
nodes.statement: \caption{Offline q-Learning Mean–Variance Algorithm with Synthetic Wealth Simulator} \textbf{Inputs}: initial state $x(0)$, horizon $T$, time step $\Delta t$, number of steps $N_T = T/\Delta t$, number of episodes $M$, number of real asset price paths $H$, number of synthetic paths (generated at each episode) $H_s$, parameterized value function $J_{\varphi}(\cdot,\cdot; w)$ and policy $\pi_{\psi}(\cdot,\cdot; w)$, initial Lagrange multiplier $w$, learning rate functions $\alpha_{\varphi}(\cdot),\alpha_{\psi}(\cdot), \alpha_w(\cdot)$ \textbf{Required program}: a real wealth simulator $x' = Wealth_{\Delta t}(t,x,a)$ that takes current time--state pair $(t,x)$ and action $a$ as inputs and generates state $x'$ at time $t + \Delta t$ according to \eqref{eq: MV_wealth_process}, a synthetic wealth simulator $x'=Wealth_{\Delta t}(t, x, a; G(\theta))$ based on synthetic paths from a generative model $G(\theta)$, q-function $q_{\psi}(t, x, a; w) = \log\pi_\psi(t, x, a; w)$. \textbf{Learning procedure}: \begin{algorithmic} \FOR{episode $m = 1$ \TO $M$} \STATE Generate $H_s$ synthetic asset price paths by $G(\theta)$. \STATE Initialize $n = 0$ and store $x^{(j)}(t_n) \leftarrow x(0)$ for $j=1,..., H + H_s$. \WHILE{$n < N_T$} \FOR{path $j=1$ \TO $H + H_s$} \STATE{Generate action $a^{(j)}(t_n)\sim \pi_{\psi}(\cdot|t_n, x^{(j)}(t_n); w)$. Compute and store the test functions \vspace{-3mm} \[ \xi^{(j)}(t_n)= \frac{\partial J_\varphi}{\partial \varphi}(t_{n},x^{(j)}(t_n); w),\quad \zeta^{(j)}(t_n) = \frac{\partial q_{\psi}}{\partial \psi}(t_{n}, x^{(j)}(t_n), a^{(j)}(t_n); w). \] \vspace{-5mm} \IF{$j \le H$} \STATE In the real wealth simulator: $x^{(j)}(t_{n + 1}) = Wealth_{\Delta t}(t_n, x^{(j)}(t_n), a^{(j)}(t_n)).$ \ELSE \STATE In the synthetic wealth simulator: $x^{(j)}(t_{n + 1}) = Wealth_{\Delta t}(t_n, x^{(j)}(t_n), a^{(j)}(t_n); G(\theta)).$ \ENDIF } \ENDFOR \STATE Update $n \leftarrow n + 1$. \ENDWHILE \STATE Store the terminal wealth $x^{(j)}(T; m) \leftarrow x^{(j)}(t_{N_T})$ for $j=1,..., H + H_s$. \STATE For path $j=1, \cdots H + H_s$, compute \vspace{-3mm} \begin{align*} \Delta \varphi^{(j)} = \sum_{n=0}^{N_T - 1} \xi^{(j)}(t_n) \big[ J_\varphi(t_{n + 1}, x^{(j)}(t_{n + 1}); w) - J_\varphi(t_n, x^{(j)}(t_n); w) -q_{\psi}(t_n, x^{(j)}(t_n) ,a^{(j)}(t_n); w)\Delta t \big],\\ \Delta \psi^{(j)} = \sum_{n=0}^{N_T - 1} \zeta^{(j)}(t_n)\big[ J_\varphi(t_{n + 1}, x^{(j)}(t_{n + 1}); w) - J_\varphi(t_n, x^{(j)}(t_n); w) - q_{\psi}(t_n, x^{(j)}(t_n), a^{(j)}(t_n); w)\Delta t \big] . \end{align*} \vspace{-3mm} \STATE Update $\varphi$ and $\psi$: $\varphi \leftarrow \varphi + \frac{\alpha_{\varphi}(m)}{H + H_s}\sum_{j=1}^{H + H_s}\Delta \varphi^{(j)},\ \psi \leftarrow \psi + \cdot\frac{\alpha_{\psi}(m)}{H + H_s} \sum_{j=1}^{H + H_s}\Delta \psi ^{(j)}$ \vspace{1mm} \STATE Update $w$ (Lagrange multiplier) every $L$ episodes: \IF{$m\equiv 0$ mod $L$} \STATE{$w\leftarrow w - \alpha_w \frac{1}{L}\sum_{i=m - L + 1}^m \frac{1}{H + H_s}\sum_{j=1}^{H + H_s}x^{(j)}(T; i)$} \ENDIF \ENDFOR \end{algorithmic}
nodes.section: D The $q-$Learning Algorithm for Continuous-Time Mean-Variance Portfolio Selection

nodes.name: FiLM conditional linear layer
nodes.statement: The output of $L(\mathbf{z}, \tau_k)\in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}}}$ is given by: \begin{align*} L(\mathbf{z}, \tau_k) = \boldsymbol{\gamma}(k) \odot (\mathbf{W}\mathbf{z} + \mathbf{b}), \end{align*} where $\mathbf{W} \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}} \times d_{\text{in}}}$ and $\mathbf{b} \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}}}$ are respectively the learnable weight and bias of the linear projection, $\boldsymbol{\gamma}: \{1, \dots, K\}\to \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}}}$ is a learnable time-step embedding vector, and $\odot$ denotes the Hadamard (element-wise) product.

nodes.name: Score network architecture
nodes.statement: The neural network $s_\theta(\tau_k, \mathbf{x}, \mathbf{c})$ is constructed by the composition of $m$ conditional linear layers $L_1, \cdots L_m$, and $m$ activation functions $A_1, \cdots, A_m$: \begin{align*} s_\theta(\tau_k, \mathbf{x}, \mathbf{c}) = A_m\circ L_m(\cdot, \tau_k)\circ A_{m - 1}\circ L_{m - 1}(\cdot, \tau_k)\circ \cdots \circ A_1\circ L_1((\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{c}), \tau_k). \end{align*}

nodes.name: Discretize time and initialize from Gaussian noise
nodes.statement: Specifically, let $\tau_k = k\Delta \tau$ and $\tilde{\mathbf{Z}}(0) \sim \mathcal{N}(0, I_d)$.
nodes.statement_short: Discretize time and initialize from Gaussian noise

nodes.name: Euler-Maruyama update with learned score
nodes.statement: For $k=0,1,\cdots,K-1$, set \begin{align} \tilde{\mathbf{Z}}(\tau_{k + 1}) = \tilde{\mathbf{Z}}(\tau_{k}) + [\tilde f(\tau_k)\tilde{\mathbf{Z}}(\tau_k) + \tilde g^2(\tau_k) s_\theta(T_g - \tau_k, \tilde{\mathbf{Z}}(\tau_{k})), \mathbf{c})]\Delta\tau + \tilde g(\tau_k)\sqrt{\Delta\tau} \cdot \zeta_k, \end{align} where $\tilde f(\tau) = f(T_g - \tau), \tilde g(\tau) = g(T_g - \tau)$, and $\zeta_k$'s are i.i.d. standard Gaussian random vectors.
nodes.statement_short: Euler-Maruyama update with learned score

nodes.name: Output terminal state
nodes.statement: The terminal state $\tilde{\mathbf{Z}}(\tau_K)$ is a generated, desired sample.
nodes.statement_short: Output terminal state

nodes.name: Introduce ACL and show target increment laws are ACL with positive density
nodes.statement: Throughout this proof, if a probability distribution is absolutely continuous w.r.t the Lebesgue measure, we simply say this distribution is ACL. We first consider the target paths. For any $t_n\in\mathcal{T}$, denote by $P_{n + 1| n}(\cdot | \mathbf{x}(t_n))$ the conditional distribution of $\mathbf{X}(t_{n + 1})$ given $\mathbf{X}(t_n) = \mathbf{x}(t_n)$, which is ACL and positive almost everywhere on $\mathbb{R}^d$ according to Assumption \ref{assumption: SDE_solution_supp_abs}(b). It follows that the conditional distribution $P_{\Delta\mathbf{X}(t_n; \mathbf{x}(t_n))}$ of the increment is also ACL and positive almost everywhere on $\mathbb{R}^d$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce ACL and show target increment laws are ACL with positive density

nodes.name: Deduce equivalence of increment law and Lebesgue measure
nodes.statement: Therefore, for any $A\subset \mathbb{R}^d$, \begin{align} \int_{\mathbf{x}\in A}1 \mathrm{d} \mathbf{x} = 0\quad \text{ if and only if }\quad \int_{\mathbf{x} \in A}1\cdot \frac{\mathrm{d} P_{\Delta\mathbf{X}(t_n; \mathbf{x}(t_n))}(\mathbf{x})}{\mathrm{d} \mathbf{x}} \mathrm{d} \mathbf{x}= 0, \end{align} where $\frac{\mathrm{d} P_{\Delta\mathbf{X}(t_n; \mathbf{x}(t_n))}(\mathbf{x})}{\mathrm{d} \mathbf{x}}$ is the Radon–Nikodym derivative (i.e., the density function) of $P_{\Delta\mathbf{X}(t_n; \mathbf{x}(t_n))}(\mathbf{x})$ w.r.t. the Lebesgue measure. This implies that $P_{\Delta\mathbf{X}(t_n; \mathbf{x}(t_n))}$ and the Lebesgue measure are equivalent.
nodes.statement_short: Deduce equivalence of increment law and Lebesgue measure

nodes.name: Markov factorization shows the target path law is ACL
nodes.statement: Next, consider $P_{1:N_T|0}$. For any $0 \le m < n\le N_T$, let $\mathbf{X}(m:n):=(\mathbf{X}(t_m), \mathbf{X}(t_{m + 1}),\cdots, \mathbf{X}(t_n))$, and denote by $P_{m:n|0}$ the joint distribution of $\mathbf{X}(m:n)$ conditional on $\mathbf{X}(t_0)\equiv\mathbf{x}(t_0)$. Let $\mathbf{x}(m:n) = (\mathbf{x}(t_m), \cdots, \mathbf{x}(t_n))$ be a realization of $\mathbf{X}(m:n)$. Due to the Markov property of the Target SDE \eqref{eq: target_SDE}, we have \begin{align} \mathrm{d} P_{m:n|0}(\mathbf{x}(m:n)) &= \mathrm{d} \bigg[P_{m|0}(\mathbf{x}(t_m))\prod_{j=m}^{n - 1}P\big(\mathbf{X}(t_{j + 1})=\mathbf{x}(t_{j + 1}) | \mathbf{X}(m:j)=\mathbf{x}(m:j)\big)\bigg] \nonumber\\ &= \mathrm{d} \bigg[P_{m|0}(\mathbf{x}(t_m))\prod_{j=m}^{n - 1}P\big(\mathbf{X}(t_{j + 1})=\mathbf{x}(t_{j + 1}) | \mathbf{X}(t_j)=\mathbf{x}(t_j)\big)\bigg] \nonumber\\ &= \mathrm{d} P_{m|0}(\mathbf{x}(t_m))\prod_{j=m}^{n - 1}\mathrm{d} P_{j + 1 | j}\big(\mathbf{x}(t_{j + 1}) | \mathbf{x}(t_j)\big), \end{align} where we recall that $P_{m|0}(\mathbf{x}(t_m))$ and $P_{j + 1 | j}\big(\mathbf{x}(t_{j + 1}) | \mathbf{x}(t_j)\big)$ are ACL and positive almost everywhere on $\mathbb{R}^d$ for any $m$ and $j$ because of Assumption \ref{assumption: SDE_solution_supp_abs}(b). Hence, $P_{m:n|0}$ is ACL and positive almost everywhere on $\mathbb{R}^{d\times (n - m + 1)}$ for any $m < n$. In particular, $P_{1:N_T|0}$ is ACL and positive almost everywhere on $\mathbb{R}^{d\times N_T}$.
nodes.statement_short: Markov factorization shows the target path law is ACL

nodes.name: Target path law equivalent to Lebesgue
nodes.statement: Using a similar argument as in \eqref{eq: equivalent_to_lebesgue}, we deduce that $P_{1:N_T|0}$ is equivalent to the Lebesgue measure.
nodes.statement_short: Target path law equivalent to Lebesgue

nodes.name: Generated increment is a sum with an independent Gaussian, hence ACL and positive
nodes.statement: On the other hand, consider the distribution of the generated increment $\hat P_{\Delta\hat{\mathbf{X}}(t_n; \mathbf{x}(t_n))}$ for a given $t_n$ and $\mathbf{x}(t_n)$. Note that $\Delta\hat{\mathbf{X}}(t_n; \mathbf{x}(t_n))$ is the terminal state (i.e. $\tilde{\mathbf{Z}}(\tau_K)$) at the last step of the generation process \eqref{eq: reverse_SDE_DDPM_simulation}, which means it is the sum of a random variable determined by the state of the second last step of \eqref{eq: reverse_SDE_DDPM_simulation} (i.e. $ \tilde{\mathbf{Z}}(\tau_{K - 1})$) and an independent Gaussian variable (with mean $0$ and variance $g^2(T_g - \tau_{K - 1})\Delta\tau \cdot I_d$). It follows that $\hat P_{\Delta\hat{\mathbf{X}}(t_n; \mathbf{x}(t_n))}$ is ACL and positive almost everywhere on $\mathbb{R}^d$ by Corollary 2.2 of \cite{bhattacharya2007basic}, and consequently also equivalent to the Lebesgue measure for each $n$.
nodes.statement_short: Generated increment is a sum with an independent Gaussian, hence ACL and positive

nodes.name: Generated path law equivalent to Lebesgue
nodes.statement: By the autoregressive generation \eqref{eq: AR_generation}, the conditional distribution $\hat P_{n + 1|n}(\cdot |\hat{\mathbf{x}}(t_n))$ of $\hat{\mathbf{X}}(t_{n + 1})$ conditional on $\hat{\mathbf{X}}(t_n)=\hat{\mathbf{x}}(t_n)$ is ACL and positive almost everywhere on $\mathbb{R}^d$ for each $n$. Using similar arguments leading to \eqref{eq: equivalent_to_lebesgue} and \eqref{eq: target_Markov}, we conclude that the distribution $\hat P_{1:N_T|0}$ of the entire generated path $\big(\hat{\mathbf{X}}(t_1, \cdots, \hat{\mathbf{X}}(t_{N_T})\big)$ is equivalent to the Lebesgue measure and positive almost everywhere on $\mathbb{R}^{d\times N_T}$.
nodes.statement_short: Generated path law equivalent to Lebesgue

nodes.name: KL chain rule with Markov property gives the decomposition
nodes.statement: Finally, we establish the decomposition result \eqref{eq: path_KL_decomposition} for the KL-divergence between the target and generated paths. Note that given $\mathbf{X}(t_0)\equiv \mathbf{x}(t_0)$, the Markov property holds for both $\mathbf{X}(1:N_T)$ and $\hat{\mathbf{X}}(1:N_T)$. Then, the chain rule of KL-divergence \citep[Exercise 3.2]{wainwright2019high} implies that \begin{align*} \text{KL}\big(P_{1:N_T|0} || \hat P_{1:N_T|0}\big) &= \sum_{n=0}^{N_T - 1}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{x}(0:n)\sim \mathbf{X}(0:n)| \mathbf{X}(t_0)} \bigg[\text{KL}\big(P_{\mathbf{X}(t_{n + 1}) |\mathbf{X}(0:n)=\mathbf{x}(0:n)} \big|\big| \hat P_{\hat{\mathbf{X}}(t_{n + 1}) |\hat{\mathbf{X}}(0:n)=\mathbf{x}(0:n)}\bigg]\\ &=\sum_{n=0}^{N_T - 1}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{x}(0:n)\sim \mathbf{X}(0:n)| \mathbf{X}(t_0)} \bigg[\text{KL}\big(P_{\mathbf{X}(t_{n + 1}) |\mathbf{X}(t_n)=\mathbf{x}(t_n)} \big|\big| \hat P_{\hat{\mathbf{X}}(t_{n + 1}) |\hat{\mathbf{X}}(t_n)=\mathbf{x}(t_n)}\bigg]\\ &= \sum_{n=0}^{N_T - 1}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{x}(t_n)\sim \mathbf{X}(t_n)| \mathbf{X}(t_0)} \bigg[\text{KL}\big(P_{\Delta\mathbf{X}(t_n; \mathbf{x}(t_n))} \big|\big| \hat P_{\Delta\hat{\mathbf{X}}(t_n; \mathbf{x}(t_n))}\bigg]\\ &= \sum_{n=0}^{N_T - 1}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{X}(t_n)\sim P_{n|0}}\bigg[\text{KL}\big(P_{\Delta\mathbf{X}(t_n; \mathbf{X}(t_n))} \big|\big| \hat P_{\Delta\hat{\mathbf{X}}(t_n; \mathbf{X}(t_n))}\big)\bigg]. \end{align*} This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: KL chain rule with Markov property gives the decomposition

nodes.name: State the KL decomposition lemma
nodes.statement:
Given a fixed condition $\mathbf{c}$, we first state Lemma ef{lemma: KL_bound_decomposition} below, which decomposes $	ext{KL} ig(p_{	ext{target}}(\cdot | \mathbf{c}) || 	ilde p^	heta_{	au_K}(\cdot | \mathbf{c}) ig)$ and identifies various sources of approximation errors.  egin{lemma} For a given condition $\mathbf{c}$, denote by $	ilde p^	heta_{	au_K}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})$ the marginal density of the generated $	ilde{\mathbf{Z}}(	au_K)$ of the reverse process \eqref{eq: reverse_SDE_DDPM_simulation}. Under the conditions of Proposition ef{prop: condition_diffusion_KL_bound}, we have  egin{align} &	ext{KL} ig(p_{	ext{target}}(\cdot | \mathbf{c}) || 	ilde p^	heta_{	au_K}(\cdot | \mathbf{c}) ig) 
onumber\ &\lesssim 	ext{KL} ig(q_{T_g}(\cdot | \mathbf{c}) || \mathcal{N}(0, I_d) ig) + \sum_{k=1}^{K} \int_{	au_{k-1}}^{	au_k}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)\sim q_	au(\cdot | \mathbf{c}), \mathbf{Y}(	au_k)\sim q_{	au_k|	au}(\cdot |\mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{c})} ig[||f(	au)\mathbf{Y}(	au) - f(	au_k)\mathbf{Y}(	au_k)||^2 ig]\mathrm{d}	au 
onumber\ &\qquad + \sum_{k=1}^{K} \int_{	au_{k-1}}^{	au_k}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)\sim q_	au(\cdot | \mathbf{c}), \mathbf{Y}(	au_k)\sim q_{	au_k | 	au}(\cdot | \mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{c})} ig[||g^2(	au)
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) - g^2(	au_k)
abla\log q_{	au_k}(\mathbf{Y}(	au_k) | \mathbf{c})||^2 ig]\mathrm{d}	au
onumber\ &\qquad + \sum_{k=1}^{K}\int_{	au_{k - 1}}^{	au_{k}}[g^2(	au_k) - g^2(	au)]^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)\sim q_{	au}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}  ig[ ig\|
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) ig\|^2 ig] \mathrm{d}	au 
onumber \ &\qquad + \Delta 	au\sum_{k=1}^{K}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}\sim q_{	au_k}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})} ig[||g^2(	au_k)
abla\log q_{	au_k}(\mathbf{Y}(	au_k) | \mathbf{c}) - g^2(	au_k)s_	heta(	au_k, \mathbf{Y}(	au_k), \mathbf{c})||^2 ig]. \end{align} \end{lemma} The proof of Lemma ef{lemma: KL_bound_decomposition} can be found in Appendix ef{sec: error_identification}. We next discuss how to bound each term on the right-hand-side of \eqref{eq: KL_bound_decomposition}.
nodes.statement_short: State the KL decomposition lemma

nodes.name: Initialization error lemma
nodes.statement: The first term of \eqref{eq: KL_bound_decomposition} is the initialization error arising from the use of the Gaussian noise, instead of the terminal state of the forward process, as the initialization of the generation process \eqref{eq: reverse_SDE_DDPM_simulation}. We bound this initialization error in Lemma \ref{lemma: initial_dist_error_bound}, leveraging on the exponential convergence property of the forward OU process \eqref{eq: forward_SDE_DDPM}. The proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma: initial_dist_error_bound} is given in Appendix \ref{sec: Gaussian_initialization_error}. \begin{lemma} For the terminal marginal density $q_{T_g}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})$ induced by the forward process defined in \eqref{eq: forward_SDE_DDPM}, if the moment condition \eqref{eq: convergence_finite_moment} is satisfied, then we have: \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{c}\sim\mathbf{C}}\bigg[\text{KL}\big(q_{T_g}(\cdot | \mathbf{c}) || \mathcal{N}(0, I_d)\big)\bigg]\lesssim e^{-\frac{a}{2}T_g^2 - bT_g}\big[M_2 + de^{-\frac{a}{2}T_g^2 - bT_g}\big]. \end{align*} \end{lemma}
nodes.statement_short: Initialization error lemma

nodes.name: State discretization error lemma
nodes.statement: Next, we bound the second term of \eqref{eq: KL_bound_decomposition}, which accounts for the state discretization error of using $f(\tau_k)\mathbf{Y}(\tau_k)$ to approximate $f(\tau)\mathbf{Y}(\tau)$ for $\tau\in[\tau_{k - 1}, \tau_k]$. Lemma \ref{lemma: state_discrete_error_bound} shows that this error can be controlled under the finite moment condition \eqref{eq: convergence_finite_moment}. The proof, deferred to Appendix \ref{sec: state_discrretization_error}, is based on applying It\^{o}'s formula to $f(\tau)\mathbf{Y}(\tau)$. \begin{lemma} For the forward process $\mathbf{Y}$ in \eqref{eq: forward_SDE_DDPM}, if the moment condition \eqref{eq: convergence_finite_moment} is satisfied, then we have: \begin{align*} &\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{c}\sim\mathbf{C}}\bigg[\sum_{k=1}^{K} \int_{\tau_{k -1}}^{\tau_k}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_\tau(\cdot | \mathbf{c}), \mathbf{Y}(\tau_k)\sim q_{\tau_k | \tau}(\cdot | \mathbf{Y}(\tau), \mathbf{c})}\big[||f(\tau)\mathbf{Y}(\tau) - f(\tau_k)\mathbf{Y}(\tau_k)||^2\big]\mathrm{d}\tau\bigg] \\ &\lesssim \Delta\tau(M_2 + d)(T_g + 1)^5. \end{align*} \end{lemma}
nodes.statement_short: State discretization error lemma

nodes.name: Score discretization error lemma
nodes.statement_short: Score discretization error lemma

nodes.name: Brownian discretization error lemma
nodes.statement: The fourth term of \eqref{eq: KL_bound_decomposition} is the discretization error of simulating the Brownian motion $g(\tau)\mathrm{d}\mathbf{B}(\tau)$ in \eqref{eq: reverse_SDE_DDPM} by $g(\tau_k)\sqrt{\Delta\tau}\zeta_k \overset{d}{=}g(\tau_k)\mathrm{d}\mathbf{B}(\tau)$ from $\tau_k$ to $\tau_{k + 1}$ in \eqref{eq: reverse_SDE_DDPM_simulation}. We provide a bound on this error in Lemma \ref{lemma: BM_discretization_error_bound}, whose proof is given in Appendix \ref{sec: BM_discrete_error}. \begin{lemma} Under the same condition as in Lemma~\ref{lemma: score_discretization_error_bound}, we have \begin{align*} &\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{c}\sim\mathbf{C}}\bigg[\sum_{k=1}^{K}\int_{\tau_{k - 1}}^{\tau_{k}}[g^2(\tau_k) - g^2(\tau)]^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_{\tau}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})} \big[\big\|\nabla\log q_\tau(\mathbf{Y}(\tau) | \mathbf{c})\big\|^2\big] \mathrm{d}\tau\bigg]\\ & \quad \lesssim d(\Delta\tau)^2[L_1 + T_g + 1]. \end{align*} \end{lemma}
nodes.statement_short: Brownian discretization error lemma

nodes.name: Bound score matching term by the score error condition
nodes.statement: The last term of \eqref{eq: KL_bound_decomposition} captures the score matching error out of the neural network approximation of the true score function. Given condition \eqref{eq: convergence_score_matching}, we have \begin{align} &\Delta \tau\sum_{k=1}^{K}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{c}\sim\mathbf{C}}\bigg[\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}\sim q_{\tau_k}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}\big[||g^2(\tau_k)\nabla\log q_{\tau_k}(\mathbf{Y}(\tau_k) | \mathbf{c}) - g^2(\tau_k)s_\theta(\tau_k, \mathbf{Y}(\tau_k), \mathbf{c})||^2\big]\bigg]\nonumber\\ &\le (T_g + 1)^3\varepsilon_{\text{score}}^2. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Bound score matching term by the score error condition

nodes.name: Combine Lemmas 1-5 and the score bound
nodes.statement: Finally, by combining the results of Lemma \ref{lemma: KL_bound_decomposition} through Lemma \ref{lemma: BM_discretization_error_bound}, along with the bound \eqref{eq: score_matching_error_bound} on the score matching error, we obtain the error bound in \eqref{eq: condition_diffusion_KL_bound}, proving Proposition \ref{prop: condition_diffusion_KL_bound}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine Lemmas 1-5 and the score bound

nodes.name: Integrate the KL derivative bound of Lemma 6(b) over a step
nodes.statement: We apply the result of Lemma \ref{lemma: KL_dt}(b) and set $C_{KL} = b$. Note that $\tilde g^2(\tau) = g^2(T_g - \tau) = a(T_g - \tau) + b \ge b$ for any $\tau\in[0, T_g]$. Then, integrating on both sides of \eqref{eq: density_KL_dt_bound} from $\tau_k$ to $\tau_{k + 1}$, we have \begin{align*} &\text{KL}\big(\tilde p_{\tau_{k + 1} | \tau_k}(\cdot | \tilde{\mathbf{z}}) || \tilde p^\theta_{\tau_{k + 1} | \tau_k}(\cdot | \tilde{\mathbf{z}}\big) - \lim_{\tau\to\tau_k+}\text{KL}\big(\tilde p_{\tau | \tau_k}(\cdot | \tilde{\mathbf{z}}) || \tilde p^\theta_{\tau | \tau_k}(\cdot | \tilde{\mathbf{z}}\big)\\ &\le \frac{1}{b}\int_{\tau_k}^{\tau_{k + 1}} \mathbb{E}_{\tilde{\mathbf{Y}}(\tau)\sim\tilde p_{\tau | \tau_k}(\cdot | \tilde{\mathbf{z}})} \big\|\tilde f(\tau)\tilde{\mathbf{Y}}(\tau) - \tilde f(\tau_k)\tilde{\mathbf{z}} + \tilde g^2(\tau)\nabla\log q_{T_g - \tau}(\tilde{\mathbf{Y}}(\tau)|\mathbf{c}) - \tilde g^2(\tau_k)s_\theta(T_g - \tau_k, \tilde{\mathbf{z}}, \mathbf{c})\big\|^2\mathrm{d} \tau\\ &\qquad + \frac{1}{4b}\int_{\tau_k}^{\tau_{k + 1}} [\tilde g^2(\tau_k) - \tilde g^2(\tau)]^2\mathbb{E}_{\tilde{\mathbf{Y}}(\tau)\sim\tilde p_{\tau | \tau_k}(\cdot | \tilde{\mathbf{z}})} \big[\big\|\nabla\log\tilde p_\tau(\tilde{\mathbf{Y}}(\tau))\big\|^2\big] \mathrm{d}\tau. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Integrate the KL derivative bound of Lemma 6(b) over a step

nodes.name: Average over the starting point using Lemma 6(a)
nodes.statement:
Since the above result holds when $	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au_k)= 	ilde{\mathbf{Z}}(	au_k) = 	ilde {\mathbf{z}}$ for any fixed $	ilde{\mathbf{z}}\in\mathbb{R}^d$, we can integrate on both sides of the above inequality w.r.t. $	ilde {\mathbf{z}} = 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au_k)\sim 	ilde p_{	au_k}$. Then, by Lemma ef{lemma: KL_dt}(a), we have  egin{align} &\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au_k)\sim 	ilde p_{	au_k}}  ig[	ext{KL} ig(	ilde p_{	au_{k + 1} | 	au_k}(\cdot | 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au_k)) || 	ilde p^	heta_{	au_{k +1} | 	au_k}(\cdot | 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au_k) ig)  ig] 
onumber\ &\le  rac{1}{b}\int_{	au_k}^{	au_{k + 1}}\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au_k), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au))} igg[ ig\|	ilde g^2(	au)
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)|\mathbf{c}) - 	ilde g^2(	au_k)s_	heta(T_g - 	au_k, 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au_k), \mathbf{c}) 
onumber\ &\qquad \qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad + 	ilde f(	au)	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) - 	ilde f(	au_k) 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au_k)  ig\|^2 igg]\mathrm{d} 	au
onumber\ &\qquad +  rac{1}{4b}\int_{	au_k}^{	au_{k + 1}} [	ilde g^2(	au_k) - 	ilde g^2(	au)]^2\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)\sim 	ilde p_	au}  ig[ ig\|
abla\log	ilde p_	au(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)) ig\|^2 ig] \mathrm{d}	au, \end{align} where the expectation in the first term on the right-hand side is taken w.r.t. $	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au_k)\sim	ilde p_{	au_k}$ and $	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)\sim	ilde p_{	au|	au_k}(\cdot | 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au_k))$.
nodes.statement_short: Average over the starting point using Lemma 6(a)

nodes.name: KL chain rule across one step
nodes.statement: On the other hand, consider the reverse SDE \eqref{eq: piece_reverse_SDE} starting from $\tilde{\mathbf{Y}}(\tau_k)\sim\tilde p_{\tau_k}$, and the simulated SDE \eqref{eq: piece_reverse_SDE_simulation} starting from $\tilde{\mathbf{Z}}(\tau_k)\sim\tilde p^\theta_{t_k}$. Using the chain rule of KL divergence, we have the following result: \begin{equation} \text{KL}\big(\tilde p_{\tau_{k + 1}} || \tilde p^\theta_{\tau_{k + 1}}\big) \le \text{KL}\big(\tilde p_{\tau_{k}} || \tilde p^\theta_{\tau_{k}}\big) + \mathbb{E}_{\tilde{\mathbf{Y}}(\tau_k)\sim\tilde p_{\tau_k}}\big[\text{KL}\big(\tilde p_{\tau_{k + 1} | \tau_k}(\cdot | \tilde{\mathbf{Y}}(\tau_k)) || \tilde p^\theta_{\tau_{k + 1} | \tau_k}(\cdot | \tilde{\mathbf{Y}}(\tau_k)\big) \big]. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: KL chain rule across one step

nodes.name: Telescope over steps and split terms
nodes.statement:
With \eqref{eq: DDPM_simulation_step_bound} and \eqref{eq: KL_chain_rule}, we have  egin{align*} &	ext{KL}(p_{	ext{target}}(\cdot | \mathbf{c}) || 	ilde p^	heta_{	au_K}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})) = 	ext{KL}(q_0(\cdot | \mathbf{c}) || 	ilde p^	heta_{	au_K}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})) = 	ext{KL} ig(	ilde p_{T_g} || 	ilde p^	heta_{	au_K} ig) = 	ext{KL} ig(	ilde p_{	au_K} || 	ilde p^	heta_{	au_K} ig)\ &\overset{\eqref{eq: KL_chain_rule}}{\le} 	ext{KL} ig(	ilde p_0 || 	ilde p^	heta_0 ig) + \sum_{k = 0}^{K - 1}\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au_k)\sim	ilde p_{	au_k}} ig[	ext{KL} ig(	ilde p_{	au_{k + 1} | 	au_k}(\cdot | 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au_k)) || 	ilde p^	heta_{	au_{k + 1} | 	au_k}(\cdot | 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au_k) ig)  ig]\ &\overset{\eqref{eq: DDPM_simulation_step_bound}}{\le} 	ext{KL} ig(q_{T_g}(\cdot | \mathbf{c}) || \mathcal{N}(0, I_d) ig) +  rac{1}{4b}\sum_{k=0}^{K - 1}\int_{	au_k}^{	au_{k + 1}}[	ilde g^2(	au_k) - 	ilde g^2(	au)]^2\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)\sim	ilde p_{	au}}  ig[ ig\|
abla\log	ilde p_	au(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)) ig\|^2 ig] \mathrm{d}	au\ &\qquad +  rac{1}{b}\sum_{k = 0}^{K - 1}\int_{	au_k}^{	au_{k + 1}}\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au_k)\sim	ilde p_{	au_k},	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)\sim	ilde p_{	au | 	au_k}(\cdot | 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au_k))} igg[ ig\|	ilde g^2(	au)
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)|\mathbf{c}) - 	ilde g^2(	au_k)s_	heta(T_g - 	au_k, 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au_k), \mathbf{c}) \ &\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad + 	ilde f(	au)	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) - 	ilde f(	au_k)	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au_k) ig\|^2 igg]\mathrm{d} 	au\ &\le 	ext{KL} ig(q_{T_g}(\cdot | \mathbf{c}) || \mathcal{N}(0, I_d) ig) +  rac{1}{4b}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\int_{	au_{k - 1}}^{	au_{k}}[g^2(	au_k) - g^2(	au)]^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)\sim q_{	au}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}  ig[ ig\|
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) ig\|^2 ig] \mathrm{d}	au\ &\qquad +  rac{1}{b}\sum_{k = 1}^{K}\int_{	au_{k - 1}}^{	au_{k}}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)\sim q_{	au}(\cdot | \mathbf{c}),\mathbf{Y}(	au_k)\sim q_{	au_k | 	au}(\cdot | \mathbf{Y}(	au_k), \mathbf{c})} igg[ ig\|g^2(	au)
abla\log q_{	au}(\mathbf{Y}(	au)|\mathbf{c}) - g^2(	au_k)s_	heta(	au_k, \mathbf{Y}(	au_k), \mathbf{c}) \ &\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad + f(	au)\mathbf{Y}(	au) - f(	au_k)\mathbf{Y}(	au_k) ig\|^2 igg]\mathrm{d} 	au\ &\lesssim 	ext{KL} ig(q_{T_g}(\cdot | \mathbf{c}) || \mathcal{N}(0, I_d) ig) + \sum_{k=1}^{K}\int_{	au_{k - 1}}^{	au_{k}}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)\sim q_{	au}(\cdot | \mathbf{c}),\mathbf{Y}(	au_k)\sim q_{	au_k | 	au}(\cdot | \mathbf{Y}(	au_k), \mathbf{c})} ig[ ig\|f(	au_k)\mathbf{Y}(	au_k) - f(	au)\mathbf{Y}(	au)  ig\|^2 ig] \mathrm{d} 	au\ &\qquad + \sum_{k=1}^{K}\int_{	au_{k - 1}}^{	au_{k}} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)\sim q_{	au}(\cdot | \mathbf{c}),\mathbf{Y}(	au_k)\sim q_{	au_k | 	au}(\cdot | \mathbf{Y}(	au_k), \mathbf{c})} ig[ ig\| g^2(	au)
abla\log q_{	au}(\mathbf{Y}(	au)|\mathbf{c}) - g^2(	au_k)
abla\log q_{	au_k}(\mathbf{Y}(	au_k)| \mathbf{c})  ig\| ig]^2\mathrm{d} 	au\ &\qquad + \sum_{k=1}^{K}\int_{	au_{k - 1}}^{	au_{k}}[g^2(	au_k) - g^2(	au)]^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)\sim q_{	au}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}  ig[ ig\|
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) ig\|^2 ig] \mathrm{d}	au\ &\qquad + \Delta	au\sum_{k=1}^{K}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_k)\sim q_{	au_k}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}  ig\| g^2(	au_k)
abla\log q_{	au_k}(\mathbf{Y}(	au_k)|\mathbf{c}) - g^2(	au_k)s_	heta(	au_k, \mathbf{Y}(	au_k), \mathbf{c})  ig\|^2, \end{align*} where the last step is obtained by adding and subtracting a term of $g^2(	au_k)
abla\log q_{	au_k}(\mathbf{Y}(	au_k) | \mathbf{c})$, and using the fact that $\|\mathbf{x} + \mathbf{y} + \mathbf{z}\|^2 \le 9\|\mathbf{x}\|^2 + 9\|\mathbf{y}\|^2 + 9\|\mathbf{z}\|^2$. The proof is hence completed.
nodes.statement_short: Telescope over steps and split terms

nodes.name: Explicit KL of a Gaussian transition to standard normal
nodes.statement: We adapt the proof of Proposition 4 of \cite{bentonnearly} to our setting where the forward OU process is time-inhomogeneous. Recall that $q_{\tau | 0}(\cdot | \mathbf{y}(0), \mathbf{c})$ is the conditional distribution of $\mathbf{Y}(\tau)$ given $\mathbf{Y}(0) = \mathbf{y}(0)$ under condition $\mathbf{c}$, and $q_{\tau | 0}(\cdot | \mathbf{y}(0), \mathbf{c}) \sim \mathcal{N}(\lambda_\tau \mathbf{Y}(0), \sigma_\tau^2I_d)$ from \eqref{eq: DDPM_conditional_relation} and \eqref{eq: forward_SDE_coeff}. Then, one can directly compute that \begin{align*} \text{KL}(q_{\tau | 0}(\cdot | \mathbf{y}(0), \mathbf{c}) || \mathcal{N}(0, I_d)) = \frac{1}{2}\big(d\log\sigma_\tau^{-2} - d + d\sigma_\tau^2 + \|\lambda_\tau\mathbf{y}(0)\|^2\big). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Explicit KL of a Gaussian transition to standard normal

nodes.name: Convexity of KL and Jensen
nodes.statement: By the convexity of the KL divergence and Jensen's inequality, we have \begin{align*} \text{KL}\big(q_{T_g}(\cdot | \mathbf{c}) || \mathcal{N}(0, I_d)\big) &= \text{KL}\bigg(\int_{\mathbf{y}(0)\in\mathbb{R}^d} q_{T_g | 0}(\cdot | \mathbf{y}(0), \mathbf{c}) \mathrm{d} q_0(\mathbf{y}(0) | \mathbf{c}) \bigg|\bigg| \mathcal{N}(0, I_d)\bigg)\\ &\le \int_{\mathbf{y}(0)\in\mathbb{R}^d}\text{KL}\big(q_{T_g | 0}(\cdot | \mathbf{y}(0), \mathbf{c}) || \mathcal{N}(0, I_d)\big)\mathrm{d} q_0(\mathbf{y}(0) | \mathbf{c})\\ & =\frac{1}{2}\bigg(d\log\sigma_{T_g}^{-2} - d + d\sigma_{T_g}^2 + \lambda_{T_g}^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(0)\sim q_{0}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}\|\mathbf{Y}(0)\|^2\bigg)\\ &\lesssim de^{-aT_g^2 - 2bT_g} + e^{-\frac{a}{2}T_g^2 - bT_g}\big(\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(0)\sim p_{\text{target}}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}\|\mathbf{Y}(0)\|^2\big) \end{align*} where we use \eqref{eq: forward_SDE_coeff} and the approximation that $-\ln(1 - x)\lesssim x + \frac{x^2}{2}$ for $x\in(-1, 1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Convexity of KL and Jensen

nodes.name: Apply the moment condition
nodes.statement: Applying condition \eqref{eq: convergence_finite_moment}, we immediately obtain \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{c}\sim\mathbf{C}}\bigg[\text{KL}\big(q_{T_g}(\cdot | \mathbf{c}) || \mathcal{N}(0, I_d)\big)\bigg] \lesssim e^{-\frac{a}{2}T_g^2 - bT_g}\big[M_2 + de^{-\frac{a}{2}T_g^2 - bT_g}\big]. \end{align*} This completes the proof of Lemma \ref{lemma: initial_dist_error_bound}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the moment condition

nodes.name: Ito's formula for $f(\tau)Y(\tau)$
nodes.statement: By It\^{o}'s formula, with $\mathbf{Y}(\tau)$ following the forward SDE \eqref{eq: forward_SDE_DDPM}, we have \begin{align*} \mathrm{d}(f(\tau)\mathbf{Y}(\tau)) = f'(\tau)\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau + f(\tau)\mathrm{d}\mathbf{Y}(\tau) = \bigg[\frac{a}{2} - \frac{1}{4}(a\tau + b)^2\bigg]\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau + \frac{1}{2}(a\tau + b)^{\frac{3}{2}}\mathrm{d} \mathbf{B}(\tau). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Ito's formula for $f(\tau)Y(\tau)$

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz bound on the increment
nodes.statement: Let $u(\tau) := \frac{a}{2} - \frac{1}{4}(a\tau + b)^2$ and $v(\tau):=\frac{1}{2}(a\tau + b)^{\frac{3}{2}}$. Then \begin{align*} &\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_\tau(\cdot | \mathbf{c}), \mathbf{Y}(\tau_k)\sim q_{\tau_k | \tau}(\cdot | \mathbf{Y}(\tau), \mathbf{c})}\big[||f(\tau)\mathbf{Y}(\tau) - f(\tau_k)\mathbf{Y}(\tau_k)||^2\big] \\ &= \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_\tau(\cdot | \mathbf{c}), (\mathbf{B})} \bigg[\bigg|\bigg|\int_{\tau}^{\tau_k}u(s)\mathbf{Y}(s)\mathrm{d} s + \int_{\tau}^{\tau_k}v(s)\mathrm{d}\mathbf{B}(s)\bigg|\bigg|^2\bigg] \\ &\lesssim \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_\tau(\cdot | \mathbf{c}), (\mathbf{B})} \bigg[\bigg|\bigg|\int_{\tau}^{\tau_k}u(s)\mathbf{Y}(s)\mathrm{d} s\bigg|\bigg|^2 + \bigg|\bigg|\int_{\tau}^{\tau_k}v(s)\mathrm{d}\mathbf{B}(s)\bigg|\bigg|^2\bigg] \\ &\lesssim d\int_{\tau}^{\tau_k}v^2(s) \mathrm{d} s+ \left(\int_{\tau}^{\tau_k}u^2(s)\mathrm{d} s\right)\left(\int_{\tau}^{\tau_k}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(s)\sim q_s(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}[||\mathbf{Y}(s)||^2]\mathrm{d} s\right) , \end{align*} where the last inequality follows from the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz bound on the increment

nodes.name: Second-moment bound for the forward process
nodes.statement: Note that $\mathbf{Y}(s) | \mathbf{Y}(0) \sim \mathcal{N}(\lambda_s\mathbf{Y}(0), \sigma_s^2I_d)$ for $\mathbf{Y}(0)\sim p_{\text{target}}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})$. Since $\lambda^2_s, \sigma_s^2\le 1$ for any $s\in[0, T_g]$, it follows that \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(s)\sim q_s(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}[||\mathbf{Y}(s)||^2] \le \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(0)\sim p_{\text{target}}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}[\|\mathbf{Y}(0)\|^2 ] + d. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Second-moment bound for the forward process

nodes.name: Sum over steps
nodes.statement: Meanwhile, given that $\int_{\tau}^{\tau_k}u^2(s)\mathrm{d} s \lesssim \int_{\tau}^{\tau_k}(s + 1)^4\mathrm{d} s \lesssim (\Delta\tau)(\tau + 1)^4$ and $\int_{\tau}^{\tau_k}v^2(s)\mathrm{d} s \lesssim (\Delta\tau)(\tau + 1)^3$, we derive \begin{align*} & \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{c}\sim\mathbf{C}}\bigg[\sum_{k=1}^{K} \int_{\tau_{k - 1}}^{\tau_k} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_\tau(\cdot | \mathbf{c}), \mathbf{Y}(\tau_k)\sim q_{\tau_k | \tau}(\cdot | \mathbf{Y}(\tau), \mathbf{c})}\big[||f(\tau)\mathbf{Y}(\tau) - f(\tau_k)\mathbf{Y}(\tau_k)||^2\big]\mathrm{d}\tau\bigg] \\ &\lesssim \sum_{k=1}^{K} \int_{\tau_{k - 1}}^{\tau_k} \bigg[d(\Delta\tau)(\tau + 1)^3 +(\Delta\tau)^2 (M_2 + d)(\tau + 1)^4\bigg]\mathrm{d}\tau \\ &\lesssim \Delta\tau(M_2 + d)\int_{0}^{T_g}(\tau + 1)^4\mathrm{d} \tau\\ &\lesssim \Delta\tau(M_2 + d)(T_g + 1)^5, \end{align*} which completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Sum over steps

nodes.name: Existence of the Lipschitz threshold time
nodes.statement: From \eqref{eq: forward_SDE_coeff}, we note that $\lambda_\tau\sigma_\tau^{-2}$ is decreasing in $\tau$, with $\lim_{\tau \to 0+}\lambda_\tau\sigma_\tau^{-2} = +\infty$ and $\lim_{\tau \to \infty}\lambda_\tau\sigma_\tau^{-2} = 0$. Hence, for the given condition $\mathbf{c}$, there must exist $\tau_0$ such that $\lambda_{\tau_0}\sigma_{\tau_0}^{-2} = 2L(\mathbf{c})$.
nodes.statement_short: Existence of the Lipschitz threshold time

nodes.name: Introduce enlarged Lipschitz constant $L_2$
nodes.statement: This allows us to apply Lemma \ref{lemma: lipschitz_score_diff_bound} for $\tau < \min\{\tau_0, \tau_{k_1}\}$. However, when $L(\mathbf{c})$ is small, $\tau_0$ can be large. To control the magnitude of (the sum of) $(\tau_k + 1)^6$ in Lemma \ref{lemma: lipschitz_score_diff_bound}, we introduce a larger Lipschitz constant \begin{align} L_2(\mathbf{c}) := L(\mathbf{c}) + \lambda_{\min\{1,T_g/2\}}\sigma_{\min\{1, T_g/2\}}^{-2}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Introduce enlarged Lipschitz constant $L_2$

nodes.name: Define $\tau_{lipz}$ and $k_0$
nodes.statement: It is clear that $\nabla\log q_0(\cdot | \mathbf{c})$ is also $L_2(\mathbf{c})$-Lipschitz continuous. We can then define \begin{align*} \tau_{lipz}(\mathbf{c}) = \max\big\{0\le \tau\le T_g: \lambda_\tau\sigma_\tau^{-2} \ge 2L_2(\mathbf{c})\big\}. \end{align*} Note that $\lambda_{\min\{1, T_g/2\}}\sigma_{\min\{1, T_g/2\}}^{-2} \le 2L_2(\mathbf{c})$ and $\lambda_\tau\sigma_\tau^{-2}$ is decreasing in $\tau$. Thus, for any given and fixed condition $\mathbf{c}$, $\tau_{lipz}(\mathbf{c}) < \min\{1, T_g/2\} \le \tau_{k_1}.$ Let $k_{0}(\mathbf{c}) = \min\{1\le k \le K: \tau_k \ge \tau_{lipz}(\mathbf{c})\}\le k_1$.
nodes.statement_short: Define $\tau_{lipz}$ and $k_0$

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 7 on small times
nodes.statement:
We can now apply Lemma ef{lemma: lipschitz_score_diff_bound} with settings of $s = 	au_1, \cdots, 	au_{k_{0}(\mathbf{c}) - 1}$ and $s = 	au_{lipz}(\mathbf{c})$. Then, for $\mathbf{Y}(	au)\sim q_{	au}(\cdot | \mathbf{c}),\mathbf{Y}(	au_k)\sim q_{	au_k | 	au}(\cdot | \mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{c})$,  egin{align*} & \sum_{k=1}^{k_{0}(\mathbf{c}) - 1}\int_{	au_{k - 1}}^{	au_{k}}\mathbb{E}_{(\mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{Y}(	au_k))}  ig[\|g^2(	au)
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) - g^2(	au_k)
abla\log q_{	au_k}(\mathbf{Y}(	au_k) | \mathbf{c})\|^2 ig]\mathrm{d} 	au \ & \qquad + \int_{	au_{k_{0}(\mathbf{c}) - 1}}^{	au_{lipz}(\mathbf{c})}\mathbb{E}_{(\mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{Y}(	au_{k_0(\mathbf{c})}))}  ig[\|g^2(	au)
