abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) - g^2(	au_{k_0(\mathbf{c})})
abla\log q_{	au_{k_0(\mathbf{c})}}(\mathbf{Y}(	au_{k_0(\mathbf{c})}) | \mathbf{c})\|^2 ig]\mathrm{d} 	au\ &\lesssim d(\Delta	au)^2L_2(\mathbf{c})(L_2(\mathbf{c}) + 1) igg[\sum_{k=1}^{k_0(\mathbf{c})} (	au_k + 1)^6 igg]\ &\lesssim d(\Delta	au)^2L_2(\mathbf{c})(L_2(\mathbf{c}) + 1)k_0(\mathbf{c}), \end{align*} where we use the fact that $	au_{k_0(\mathbf{c})}\le 	au_{k_1} \le 1 + \Delta	au$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 7 on small times

nodes.name: Estimate $\tau_{lipz}$ and $k_0$
nodes.statement: Note that when $\tau = \tau_{lipz}(\mathbf{c})\le 1$, we can apply \eqref{eq: expoenetial_approximation} to obtain \begin{align*} 2L_2(\mathbf{c}) \asymp \frac{\lambda_\tau}{\sigma_\tau^2} = \frac{e^{-\frac{a}{4}\tau^2 - \frac{b}{2}\tau}}{1 - e^{-\frac{a}{2}\tau^2 - b\tau}} \asymp \frac{1 - a\tau^2/4 - b\tau /2}{a\tau^2/2 + b\tau} = \frac{1}{a\tau^2/2 + b\tau} - \frac{1}{2} \asymp \frac{1}{\tau} - \frac{1}{2}, \end{align*} yielding \begin{align} \tau_{lipz}(\mathbf{c}) \asymp \frac{2}{4L_2(\mathbf{c}) + 1},\quad k_0(\mathbf{c}) \asymp \frac{2}{(4L_2(\mathbf{c}) + 1)\Delta\tau}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Estimate $\tau_{lipz}$ and $k_0$

nodes.name: Small-time part bounded by $d\Delta\tau(L_1+1)$
nodes.statement:
Therefore,  egin{align} & \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{c}\sim\mathbf{C}} igg[\sum_{k=1}^{k_{0}(\mathbf{c}) - 1}\int_{	au_{k - 1}}^{	au_{k}}\mathbb{E}_{(\mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{Y}(	au_k))}  ig[\|g^2(	au)
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) - g^2(	au_k)
abla\log q_{	au_k}(\mathbf{Y}(	au_k) | \mathbf{c})\|^2 ig]\mathrm{d} 	au igg] 
onumber\ & \quad + \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{c}\sim\mathbf{C}} igg[\int_{	au_{k_{0}(\mathbf{c}) - 1}}^{	au_{lipz}(\mathbf{c})}\mathbb{E}_{(\mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{Y}(	au_{k_0(\mathbf{c})}))}  ig[\|g^2(	au)
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) - g^2(	au_{k_0(\mathbf{c})})
abla\log q_{	au_{k_0(\mathbf{c})}}(\mathbf{Y}(	au_{k_0(\mathbf{c})}) | \mathbf{c})\|^2 ig]\mathrm{d} 	au igg] 
onumber\ &\lesssim \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{c}\sim\mathbf{C}} ig[d(\Delta	au)^2L_2(\mathbf{c})(L_2(\mathbf{c}) + 1)k_0(\mathbf{c}) ig] 
onumber\ &\overset{\eqref{eq: lipz_index_approximation}}{\lesssim} d\Delta	au\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{c}\sim\mathbf{C}} ig[L_2(\mathbf{c}) + 1 ig]
onumber\ &= d\Delta	au\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{c}\sim\mathbf{C}} ig[L(\mathbf{c}) + \lambda_{\min\{1, T_g/2\}}\sigma_{\min\{1, T_g/2\}}^{-2} + 1 ig] 
onumber\ &\lesssim d\Delta	au(L_1 + 1), \end{align} where $L_1$ is defined in \eqref{eq: convergence_lipschitz}, and the last step follows from the approximation that  egin{align} \lambda_{\min\{1, T_g/2\}}\sigma_{\min\{1, T_g/2\}}^{-2} \asymp  rac{1}{a(\min\{1, T_g/2\})^2/2 + b\min\{1, T_g/2\}} -  rac{1}{2} \asymp 1. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Small-time part bounded by $d\Delta\tau(L_1+1)$

nodes.name: Large-time part via Lemma 8; combine
nodes.statement:
On the other hand, for those $k \ge k_0(\mathbf{c})$, Lemma ef{lemma: score_diff_bound_large_t} implies that  egin{align} & \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{c}\sim\mathbf{C}} igg[\int_{	au_{lipz}(\mathbf{c})}^{	au_{k_0(\mathbf{c})}} \mathbb{E}_{(\mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{Y}(	au_{k_0(\mathbf{c})}))} ig[\|g^2(	au)
abla\log q_{	au}(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) - g^2(	au_{k_0(\mathbf{c})})
abla\log q_{	au_{k_0(\mathbf{c})}}(\mathbf{Y}(	au_{k_0(\mathbf{c})}) | \mathbf{c} ) \|^2 ig] \mathrm{d}	au igg]
onumber\ & \quad + \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{c}\sim\mathbf{C}} igg[\sum_{k=k_0(\mathbf{c}) + 1}^{K }\int_{	au_{k - 1}}^{	au_k}\mathbb{E}_{(\mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{Y}(	au_k))} ig[\|g^2(	au)
abla\log q_{	au}(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) - g^2(	au_k)
abla\log q_{	au_k}(\mathbf{Y}(	au_k) | \mathbf{c} ) \|^2 ig] \mathrm{d}	au igg]
onumber\ &\lesssim \Delta	au (T_g + 1)^2 \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{c}\sim\mathbf{C}}  ig[\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(0)\sim p_{	ext{target}}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}  ig[\|\mathbf{Y}(0)\|^2 ig] ig] + d\Delta	au\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{c}\sim\mathbf{C}} igg[\ln igg( rac{1}{	au_{lipz}(\mathbf{c})}  igg) +  rac{1}{	au_{lipz}(\mathbf{c})} + (T_g + 1)^4  igg] 
onumber\ &\overset{\eqref{eq: lipz_index_approximation}}{\lesssim} M_2\Delta	au (T_g + 1)^2 + d\Delta	au \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{c}\sim\mathbf{C}} ig[\ln(2L_2(\mathbf{c}) + 1/2) + 2L_2(\mathbf{c}) + 1/2 + (T_g + 1)^4  ig] 
onumber\ &\lesssim M_2\Delta	au (T_g + 1)^2 + d\Delta	au  ig[L_1 + (T_g + 1)^4  ig], \end{align} where in the last step we use the fact that $\ln(x + 1/2) \le x + 1/2$ for any $x\ge 0$ and the approximation in \eqref{eq: threshold_approximation}. The proof is complete by combining \eqref{eq: score_error_bound_1} and \eqref{eq: score_error_bound_2}.
nodes.statement_short: Large-time part via Lemma 8; combine

nodes.name: Split the score difference into schedule and spatial parts
nodes.statement:
Given a condition $\mathbf{c}$, we can compute, for $	au < 	au_k, \mathbf{Y}(	au)\sim q_	au(\cdot | \mathbf{c})$ and $\mathbf{Y}(	au_k)\sim q_{	au_k | 	au}(\cdot | \mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{c})$,  egin{align} & \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)\sim q_	au(\cdot | \mathbf{c}), \mathbf{Y}(	au_k)\sim q_{	au_k | 	au}(\cdot | \mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{c})} ig[\|g^2(	au)
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) - g^2(	au_k)
abla\log q_{	au_k}(\mathbf{Y}(	au_k) | \mathbf{c})\|^2 ig]
onumber\ &\le 2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)} ig[\|(g^2(	au) - g^2(	au_k))
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c})\|^2] 
onumber\ &\qquad + 2\mathbb{E}_{(\mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{Y}(	au_k))} ig[g^4(	au_k)\|
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) - 
abla\log q_{	au_k}(\mathbf{Y}(	au_k) | \mathbf{c})\|^2 ig]
onumber\ &\overset{	ext{(i)}}{\le} 2 ig[ ig(g^2(	au) - g^2(	au_k) ig)^2 + 2g^4(	au_k) ig(\lambda_{	au, 	au_k}^{-1} - 1 ig)^2 ig] \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)} ig[\|
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c})\|^2]
onumber\ &\qquad + 8\mathbb{E}_{(\mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{Y}(	au_k))} ig[g^4(	au_k)\|
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) - 
abla\log q_{	au}(\lambda_{	au, 	au_k}^{-1}\mathbf{Y}(	au_k) | \mathbf{c})\|^2 ig]
onumber\ &\overset{	ext{(ii)}}{\lesssim} (	au_k - 	au)^2(	au_k + 1)^4 \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)} ig[\|
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c})\|^2]
onumber\ &\qquad + (	au_k + 1)^2\mathbb{E}_{(\mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{Y}(	au_k))} ig[\|
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) - 
abla\log q_{	au}(\lambda_{	au, 	au_k}^{-1}\mathbf{Y}(	au_k) | \mathbf{c})\|^2 ig] \end{align} where the inequality (i) is from Lemma 11 of \cite{chen2023improved}, and the inequality (ii) employs the approximation that for small $	au_k - 	au$,  egin{align*} \lambda^{-1}_{	au, 	au_k} - 1 = e^{ rac{a}{4}(	au_k^2 - 	au^2) +  rac{b}{2}(	au_k - 	au)} - 1\lesssim  rac{a}{4}(	au_k^2 - 	au^2) +  rac{b}{2}(	au_k - 	au) \lesssim (	au_k - 	au)(	au_k + 1). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Split the score difference into schedule and spatial parts

nodes.name: Lipschitz score bound for small times
nodes.statement:
Next, from the condition that $\sigma_{s}^2\le  rac{\lambda_{s}}{2L(\mathbf{c})}$ and the fact that $\lambda_	au\sigma_	au^{-2}$ is decreasing in $	au$, we know that $\sigma_{	au}^2\le  rac{\lambda_{	au}}{2L(\mathbf{c})}$ for all $	au \le s$, indicating that Lemma 14 of \cite{chen2023improved} holds and $
abla\log q_	au(\cdot | \mathbf{c})$ is $(2L(\mathbf{c})\lambda_	au^{-1})$-Lipschitz on $\mathbb{R}^d$ for all $	au \le s$. Then,  egin{align*} &\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)\sim q_	au(\cdot | \mathbf{c}), \mathbf{Y}(	au_k)\sim q_{	au_k | 	au}(\cdot | \mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{c})}[\|
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) - 
abla\log q_{	au}(\lambda_{	au, 	au_k}^{-1}\mathbf{Y}(	au_k) | \mathbf{c})\|^2] \ &\le 4L^2(\mathbf{c})\lambda_	au^{-2}\mathbb{E}_{(\mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{Y}(	au_k))}  ig[\|\mathbf{Y}(	au) - \lambda_{	au, 	au_k}^{-1} \mathbf{Y}(	au_k)\|^2 ig]\ &= 4dL^2(\mathbf{c})\lambda_	au^{-2} \lambda_{	au,	au_k}^{-2} \sigma^2_{	au, 	au_k} = 4d L^2(\mathbf{c})e^{ rac{a}{2}	au_k^2 + b	au_k} ig[1 - e^{- rac{a}{2}(	au_k^2 - 	au^2) - b(	au_k - 	au)} ig]\ &\overset{\eqref{eq: expoenetial_approximation}}{\lesssim} d L^2(\mathbf{c})(1 + a	au_k^2/2 + b	au_k)\cdot(	au_k - 	au)(a	au_k + b) \ &\lesssim d L^2(\mathbf{c})(	au_k - 	au)(	au_k + 1)^3, \end{align*} where we use the condition that $k \le k_1$ so that we can apply \eqref{eq: expoenetial_approximation} to approximate $(\lambda_	au \lambda_{	au,	au_k})^{-2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Lipschitz score bound for small times

nodes.name: Integrate over the interval
nodes.statement:
Next, the Lipschitz continuity of $
abla\log q_	au(\cdot | \mathbf{c})$ implies that $\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)\sim q_	au(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}||
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c})\|^2 \le 2dL(\mathbf{c})\lambda_	au^{-1}$ as in Lemma 21 of \cite{chen2023improved}. Hence, we can infer from \eqref{eq: score_error_target} that  egin{align*} & \int_{	au_{k - 1}}^{s}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)\sim q_	au(\cdot | \mathbf{c}), \mathbf{Y}(	au_k)\sim q_{	au_k | 	au}(\cdot | \mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{c})} ig[\|g^2(	au)
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) - g^2(	au_k)
abla\log q_{	au_k}(\mathbf{Y}(	au_k) | \mathbf{c})\|^2 ig]\mathrm{d} 	au \ &\lesssim \int_{	au_{k - 1}}^{s}(	au_k - 	au)^2(	au_k + 1)^4 dL(\mathbf{c})\lambda_	au^{-1} + d L^2(\mathbf{c})(	au_k - 	au)(	au_k + 1)^5 \mathrm{d} 	au\ &\lesssim \int_{	au_{k - 1}}^{s}(	au_k - 	au)^2(	au_k + 1)^6 dL(\mathbf{c}) + d L^2(\mathbf{c})(	au_k - 	au)(	au_k + 1)^5 \mathrm{d} 	au\ &\lesssim d(\Delta	au)^2L(\mathbf{c})(L(\mathbf{c}) + 1)(	au_k + 1)^6, \end{align*} where the second inequality is obtained by applying \eqref{eq: expoenetial_approximation} to approximate $\lambda_	au^{-1}$. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate over the interval

nodes.name: Shifted grid $\tau'_k$
nodes.statement: For notational simplicity, we introduce \begin{align*} \tau'_{k_0 - 1} = s,\ \tau'_{k} = \tau_k,\ \text{for }k=k_0, \cdots, K, \end{align*} which means that $\tau_{k}' - \tau_{k - 1}' \le \Delta\tau$ for any $k=k_0, \cdots, K$.
nodes.statement_short: Shifted grid $\tau'_k$

nodes.name: Split score difference using Lemma 9
nodes.statement:
Now, given the condition $\mathbf{c}$, note that for $\mathbf{Y}(	au)\sim q_	au(\cdot | \mathbf{c})$ and $\mathbf{Y}(	au_k')\sim q_{	au_k' | 	au}(\cdot | \mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{c})$,  egin{align*} & \mathbb{E}_{(\mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{Y}(	au_k'))}  ig[\|g^2(	au)
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) - g^2(	au_k')
abla\log q_{	au_k'}(\mathbf{Y}(	au_k') | \mathbf{c})\|^2 ig]\ &\le 2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)} ig[\|(g^2(	au) - g^2(	au_k'))
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c})\|^2]\ &\qquad + 2\mathbb{E}_{(\mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{Y}(	au_k'))}  ig[g^4(	au_k')\|
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) - 
abla\log q_{	au_k'}(\mathbf{Y}(	au_k') | \mathbf{c})\|^2 ig]\ &\lesssim d(\Delta	au)^2\sigma_	au^{-2} + \mathbb{E}_{(\mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{Y}(	au_k'))}  ig[g^4(	au_k')\|
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) - 
abla\log q_{	au_k'}(\mathbf{Y}(	au_k') | \mathbf{c})\|^2 ig], \end{align*} where the last inequality is from Lemma ef{lemma: score_function_norm_bound}.
nodes.statement_short: Split score difference using Lemma 9

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 10 to get two parts
nodes.statement:
Then, since $	au_k' = 	au_k$ for $k\ge k_0$, by Lemma ef{lemma: stochastic_char_score_diff} we have  egin{align} & \int_{s}^{	au_{k_0}}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)\sim q_	au(\cdot | \mathbf{c}), \mathbf{Y}(	au_{k_0})\sim q_{	au_{k_0} | 	au}(\cdot | \mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{c})} ig[\|g^2(	au)
abla\log q_{	au}(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) - g^2(	au_{k_0})
abla\log q_{	au_{k_0}}(\mathbf{Y}(	au_{k_0}) | \mathbf{c} ) \|^2 ig] \mathrm{d}	au
onumber\ &\qquad + \sum_{k=k_0 + 1}^{K}\int_{	au_{k - 1}}^{	au_k}\mathbb{E}_{(\mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{Y}(	au_k))} ig[\|g^2(	au)
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) - g^2(	au_k)
abla\log q_{	au_k}(\mathbf{Y}(	au_k) | \mathbf{c})\|^2 ig]\mathrm{d} 	au 
onumber\ &=\sum_{k=k_0}^{K}\int_{	au_{k - 1}'}^{	au_k'}\mathbb{E}_{(\mathbf{Y}(	au), \mathbf{Y}(	au_k'))} ig[\|g^2(	au)
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) - g^2(	au_k')
abla\log q_{	au_k'}(\mathbf{Y}(	au_k') | \mathbf{c})\|^2 ig]\mathrm{d} 	au 
onumber\ & \lesssim \sum_{k=k_0}^{K} \int_{	au_{k -1}'}^{	au_k'}  igg[d(\Delta	au)^2\sigma_	au^{-2} + \int_{	au}^{	au_k'}g^4(	au_k')f(s)d\sigma^{-2}_{	au_k'} + g^4(	au_k')g^2(s)d\sigma^{-4}_{s} \mathrm{d} s  igg]\mathrm{d} 	au \ &\qquad + \sum_{k=k_0}^{K}\int_{	au_{k - 1}'}^{	au_k'} g^4(	au_k') ig(\sigma_{	au_k'}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_k')}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au_k'})] - \sigma_{	au}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au})] ig) \mathrm{d}	au, \end{align} where we omit the dependency of $ oldsymbol{\Sigma}_	au$ on $\mathbf{Y}(	au)$ and $\mathbf{c}$ for simplicity since the context is clear.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 10 to get two parts

nodes.name: Bound the first part
nodes.statement:
We first bound \eqref{eq: score_diff_part_1}. Recall that $f(	au) =  rac{1}{2}(a	au + b), g(	au) = \sqrt{a	au + b}$. In addition, $\sigma_	au^{-2}$ is decreasing in $	au$ from \eqref{eq: forward_SDE_coeff} and we have its approximation based on \eqref{eq: expoenetial_approximation}. Then  egin{align} &\sum_{k=k_0}^{K} \int_{	au_{k -1}'}^{	au_k'}  igg[d(\Delta	au)^2\sigma_	au^{-2} + \int_{	au}^{	au_k'}g^4(	au_k')f(s)d\sigma^{-2}_{	au_k'} + g^4(	au_k')g^2(s)d\sigma^{-4}_{s} \mathrm{d} s  igg]\mathrm{d} 	au 
onumber\ &\lesssim \sum_{k=k_0}^{K}\int_{	au_{k - 1}'}^{	au_k'}  igg[d(\Delta	au)^2\sigma_{	au_{k - 1}'}^{-2} + \int_{	au}^{	au_k'} g^4(	au_k')f(	au_k')d\sigma^{-2}_{	au_{k - 1}'} + g^4(	au_k')g^2(	au_k')d\sigma^{-4}_{	au_{k - 1}'} \mathrm{d} s  igg]\mathrm{d} 	au 
onumber\ &\lesssim \sum_{k=k_0}^{k_1}  igg[ rac{d(\Delta	au)^3}{a(	au_{k - 1}')^2/2 + b	au_{k - 1}'}+  rac{d(\Delta	au)^2(a	au_k' + b)^3}{a(	au_{k - 1}')^2/2 + b	au_{k - 1}'} +  rac{d(\Delta	au)^2(a	au_k' + b)^3}{[a(	au_{k - 1}')^2/2 + b	au_{k - 1}']^2} igg] + \sum_{k_1 + 1}^{K} d(\Delta	au)^2(a	au_k' + b)^3
onumber\ &\lesssim d\Delta	au\int_{	au_{k_0 - 1}'}^{	au_{k_1}'}  igg[1 + 	au +  rac{1}{	au} +  rac{1}{	au^2} igg] \mathrm{d}	au + d\Delta	au\int_{	au_{k_1}'}^{T_g} (	au + 1)^3 \mathrm{d}	au
onumber\ &\lesssim d\Delta	au igg[\ln igg( rac{1}{	au_{k_0 - 1}'}  igg) +  rac{1}{	au_{k_0 - 1}'} + (T_g + 1)^4  igg]
onumber\ &= d\Delta	au igg[\ln igg( rac{1}{s}  igg) +  rac{1}{s} + (T_g + 1)^4  igg]. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the first part

nodes.name: Rearrange the trace telescoping sum
nodes.statement:
We next bound \eqref{eq: score_diff_part_2}. Noting that both $\sigma_	au^2$ and $\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au})]$ are increasing in $	au$ (see \eqref{eq: posterior_cov_trace_dt} and the discussion thereafter), we rearrange the summation to have  egin{align} &\sum_{k=k_0}^{K}\int_{	au_{k - 1}'}^{	au_k'}g^4(	au_k')  ig(\sigma_{	au_k'}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_k')}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au_k}')] - \sigma_{	au}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au})] ig)\mathrm{d}	au 
onumber\ &\le \sum_{k=k_0}^{K}g^4(	au_k')\Delta	au  ig(\sigma_{	au_k'}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_k')}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au_k'})] - \sigma_{	au_k'}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_{k - 1}')}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au_{k - 1}'})] ig)
onumber\ &\lesssim \sum_{k=k_0 - 1}^{k_1} \Delta	au\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_k')}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au_k'})]  ig(g^4(	au_k')\sigma_{	au_k'}^{-4} - g^4(	au_{k + 1}')\sigma_{	au_{k + 1}'}^{-4} ig) 
onumber\ &\qquad + g^4(T_g)\sigma_{	au_{k_1}'}^{-4}\Delta	au \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_{k_1 + 1}')}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au_{k_1 + 1}'})] 
onumber\ &\qquad + g^4(T_g)\sigma_{	au_{k_1}'}^{-4}\Delta	au  igg[\sum_{k=k_1 + 2}^{K} ig(\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_{k}')}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au_{k}'})] - \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_{k - 1}')}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au_{k - 1}'})] ig) igg] 
onumber\ &\overset{\eqref{eq: expoenetial_approximation}}{\lesssim} \Delta	au(T_g + 1)^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(T_g)}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{T_g})] 
onumber\ &\qquad +\sum_{k=k_0 - 1}^{k_1} \Delta	au\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_k')}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au_k'})] igg[ rac{(a	au_k' + b)^2}{[a(	au_k')^2/2 + b	au_k']^{2}} -  rac{(a	au_{k + 1}' + b)^2}{[a(	au_{k + 1}')^2/2 + b	au_{k + 1}']^{2}} igg] 
onumber\ &\lesssim \Delta	au(T_g + 1)^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(T_g)}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{T_g})] + \sum_{k=k_0 - 1}^{k_1} \Delta	au\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_k')}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au_k'})]\cdot igg[ rac{1}{(	au_k')^2} -  rac{1}{(	au_{k + 1}')^2} igg] 
onumber\ &\lesssim \Delta	au(T_g + 1)^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(T_g)}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{T_g})] + \sum_{k=k_0 - 1}^{k_1}  rac{(\Delta	au)^2}{(	au_k')^3}\cdot\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_k')}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au_k'})]. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Rearrange the trace telescoping sum

nodes.name: Bound terminal posterior trace by second moment
nodes.statement: Recall that $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\tau} = \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\tau}(\mathbf{Y}(\tau), \mathbf{c})$ is the conditional variance of $\mathbf{Y}(0)$ given $\mathbf{Y}(\tau)$ and $\mathbf{c}$. Then \begin{align} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(T_g)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{T_g})] \le \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(T_g)}\big[\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(0)|\mathbf{Y}(T_g)}\|\mathbf{Y}(0)\|^2\big] = \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(0)\sim p_{\text{target}}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}\big[\|\mathbf{Y}(0)\|^2\big]. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Bound terminal posterior trace by second moment

nodes.name: Bound posterior trace for small times
nodes.statement:
On the other hand, $\mathbf{Y}(	au) | \mathbf{Y}(0) \sim \mathcal{N} ig(\lambda_	au\mathbf{Y}(0), \sigma_	au^2I_d ig)$ from \eqref{eq: DDPM_conditional_relation}. Then, for $	au < 	au_{k_1}' = 	au_{k_1}$ in \eqref{eq: expoenential_threshold}, using a similar approximation as in \eqref{eq: expoenetial_approximation} we have  egin{align} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au})] &= \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)} ig[	ext{trace} ig({	ext{Cov}}_{\mathbf{Y}(0)|\mathbf{Y}(	au)}[\mathbf{Y}(0)] ig) ig]
onumber\ &=\lambda_{	au}^{-2}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)}  ig[	ext{trace} ig({	ext{Cov}}_{\mathbf{Y}(0)|\mathbf{Y}(	au)}[\lambda_{	au}\mathbf{Y}(0) - \mathbf{Y}(	au)] ig) ig] 
onumber\ &\le \lambda_{	au}^{-2}\mathbb{E}_{(\mathbf{Y}(0), \mathbf{Y}(	au))}  ig[\|\lambda_{	au}\mathbf{Y}(0) - \mathbf{Y}(	au)\|^2 ig] 
onumber\ &= \lambda_	au^{-2}d\sigma_	au^2 = d ig(e^{a	au^2/2 + b	au} - 1 ig)
onumber\ &\asymp d(a	au^2/2 + b	au). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Bound posterior trace for small times

nodes.name: Substitute and combine
nodes.statement:
Substituting \eqref{eq: posterior_trace_bound_1} and \eqref{eq: posterior_trace_bound_2} into \eqref{eq: posterior_trace_diff}, we have  egin{align} &\sum_{k=k_0}^{K}\int_{	au_{k - 1}'}^{	au_k'}g^4(	au_k')  ig(\sigma_{	au_k'}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au_k')}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au_k'})] - \sigma_{	au}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(	au)}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{	au})] ig)\mathrm{d}	au 
onumber\ &\lesssim \Delta	au(T_g + 1)^2 \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(0)} ig[\|\mathbf{Y}(0)\|^2 ig] + \sum_{k=k_0 - 1}^{k_1}  rac{(\Delta	au)^2d[a(	au_k')^2/2 + b	au_k' ]}{(	au_k')^3} 
onumber \ &\lesssim \Delta	au(T_g + 1)^2 \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(0)} ig[\|\mathbf{Y}(0)\|^2 ig] + d\Delta	au \int_{	au_{k_0 - 1}'}^{	au_{k_1}'} igg[ rac{1}{	au} +  rac{1}{	au^2} igg] \mathrm{d}	au 
onumber\ &\lesssim \Delta	au(T_g + 1)^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(0)} ig[\|\mathbf{Y}(0)\|^2 ig] + d\Delta	au igg[\ln igg( rac{1}{	au_{k_0 - 1}'}  igg) +  rac{1}{	au_{k_0 - 1}'} igg]
onumber\ &= \Delta	au(T_g + 1)^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(0)\sim p_{	ext{target}}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})} ig[\|\mathbf{Y}(0)\|^2 ig] + d\Delta	au igg[\ln igg( rac{1}{s}  igg) +  rac{1}{s} igg]. \end{align} The proof is complete by combining \eqref{eq: score_diff_bound_1} and \eqref{eq: score_diff_bound_2}.
nodes.statement_short: Substitute and combine

nodes.name: Recall the reverse SDE
nodes.statement: Following \cite{bentonnearly}, we first consider the stochastic dynamic of the score function $\big\{\nabla\log q_{T_g - \tau}(\tilde{\mathbf{Y}}(\tau) | \mathbf{c} ): \tau\in[0, T_g)\big\}$ under a given condition $\mathbf{c}$. Recall that the reverse SDE \eqref{eq: reverse_SDE_DDPM} of diffusion models is \begin{align*} \mathrm{d}\tilde{\mathbf{Y}}(\tau) = [\tilde f(\tau)\tilde{\mathbf{Y}}(\tau) + \tilde g^2(\tau) \nabla\log q_{T_g - \tau}(\tilde {\mathbf{Y}}(\tau) | \mathbf{c})]\mathrm{d}\tau + \tilde g(\tau) \mathrm{d}\tilde{\mathbf{B}}(\tau), \end{align*} where $\tilde f(\tau) := f(T_g - \tau)$ and $\tilde g(\tau) := g(T_g - \tau)$.
nodes.statement_short: Recall the reverse SDE

nodes.name: Ito's formula for the score process
nodes.statement:
As in the proof of Lemma 3 of \cite{bentonnearly}, $
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})$ is smooth for $	au\in[0, T_g)$, and by It\^{o}'s formula we can write  egin{align} \mathrm{d} ig[
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) ig] &=  igg\{
abla^2\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} )\cdot ig[	ilde f(	au)	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) + 	ilde g^2(	au) 
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde {\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) ig]
onumber\ &\qquad \quad +  rac{1}{2}	ilde g^2(	au)\cdot \Delta  ig(
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) ig) igg\}\mathrm{d}	au +  rac{\mathrm{d} ig[
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) ig]}{\mathrm{d} 	au} \mathrm{d} 	au 
onumber\ &\qquad + 	ilde g(	au)
abla^2\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) \mathrm{d}	ilde{\mathbf{B}}(	au). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Ito's formula for the score process

nodes.name: Fokker-Planck gives the time derivative of the score
nodes.statement:
To further simplify \eqref{eq: score_function_ito}, consider the Fokker–Planck equation for the forward process \eqref{eq: forward_SDE_DDPM}:  egin{align*} \mathrm{d} q_	au(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c}) =  igg(-
abla\cdot ig[(-f(	au)q_	au(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c})\mathbf{y}  ig] +  rac{1}{2}\Delta ig[g^2(	au)q_	au(\mathbf{y}|\mathbf{c}) ig] igg)\mathrm{d}	au, \end{align*} leading to  egin{align*} \mathrm{d}(\log q_	au(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c})) &=  rac{1}{q_	au(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c})} igg(-
abla\cdot ig[(-f(	au) q_	au(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c})\mathbf{y} ig] +  rac{1}{2} \Delta ig[g^2(	au)q_	au(\mathbf{y}|\mathbf{c}) ig] igg)\mathrm{d}	au\ &=  igg(f(	au)d + f(	au)\mathbf{y}^T
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c}) +  rac{1}{2}g^2(	au)\Delta\log q_	au(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c}) +  rac{1}{2}g^2(	au)\|
abla\log q_	au(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c})\|^2 igg)\mathrm{d} 	au. \end{align*} It follows that  egin{equation}  egin{split} & rac{\mathrm{d} ig[
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c} ) ig]}{\mathrm{d} 	au} = 
abla rac{\mathrm{d}(\log q_{T_g - 	au}(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c}))}{\mathrm{d} 	au} \ &= - igg(	ilde f(	au)
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c}) + 	ilde f(	au)
abla^2\log q_{T_g - 	au}(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c})\cdot\mathbf{y} \ & \quad \qquad +  rac{1}{2}	ilde g^2(	au)
abla ig(\Delta\log q_{T_g - 	au}(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c}) ig) + 	ilde g^2(	au)
abla^2\log q_{T_g - 	au}(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c})\cdot 
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c}) igg). \end{split} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Fokker-Planck gives the time derivative of the score

nodes.name: Simplified score SDE
nodes.statement:
Substituting \eqref{eq: score_function_time_derivative} into \eqref{eq: score_function_ito} and simplifying, we obtain  egin{align} \mathrm{d} ig[
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) ig] = -	ilde f(	au)
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) \mathrm{d} 	au + 	ilde g(	au)
abla^2\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) \mathrm{d}	ilde{\mathbf{B}}(	au). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Simplified score SDE

nodes.name: Cross-term derivative using Lemma 11 martingale property
nodes.statement:
Now, we establish the desired bound. First, for fixed $s \in (0, 	au)$, we have  egin{align*} &\mathrm{d} ig[(
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} ))^T
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) ig] \ &= -	ilde f(	au)(
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} ))^T
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c}) \mathrm{d} 	au \ &\qquad + 	ilde g(	au)(
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} ))^T
abla^2\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) \mathrm{d}	ilde{\mathbf{B}}(	au). \end{align*} By Lemma ef{lemma: hessian_score_bound}, $\int_{s}^	au \mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(u)} ig[\|
abla^2\log q_{T_g - u}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(u))\|^2_F ig]\mathrm{d} u < \infty$ where $	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(u)\sim q_{T_g - u}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})$, implying that the final term in the above equation is a square-integrable martingale. Integrating on both sides and taking expectations w.r.t. the joint distribution of $(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s))$ induced by \eqref{eq: reverse_SDE_DDPM}, we get  egin{equation}  egin{split} & rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}	au}\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s))} ig[(
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} ))^T
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) ig]\ &= -\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s))} ig[	ilde f(	au)(
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} ))^T
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c})  ig]. \end{split} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Cross-term derivative using Lemma 11 martingale property

nodes.name: Ito isometry gives the Frobenius-norm characterization
nodes.statement:
Next, if setting $	ilde\Lambda(	au) = \exp ig(\int_0^	au 	ilde f(s)\mathrm{d} s  ig)$ and applying It\^{o}'s formula to \eqref{eq: score_function_process}, we obtain  egin{align*} \mathrm{d} ig[	ilde\Lambda(	au)
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) ig] = 	ilde\Lambda(	au)	ilde g(	au)
abla^2\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) \mathrm{d}	ilde{\mathbf{B}}(	au). \end{align*} We know from Lemma ef{lemma: hessian_score_bound} that $\int_{s}^	au	ilde\Lambda^2(u)\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(u)}  ig[\|
abla^2\log q_{T_g - u}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(u))\|^2_F ig]\mathrm{d} u < \infty$ for any fixed $s > 0$. By It\^{o}'s isometry and chain rule, we obtain  egin{align*} &	ilde\Lambda^2(	au)	ilde g^2(	au)\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)} ig[\|
abla^2\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c})\|^2_F ig]\ &=  rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}	au}\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s))} ig[\|	ilde\Lambda(	au)
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) - 	ilde\Lambda(s)
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} )\|^2 ig] 
onumber\ &= 	ilde\Lambda^2(	au)\cdot  rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}	au}\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)} ig[\|
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) ||^2 + 2	ilde f(	au)	ilde\Lambda^2(	au) \mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)} ig[\|
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) ||^2\ &\qquad - 2	ilde\Lambda(	au)	ilde\Lambda(s)\cdot  rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}	au}\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s))} ig[(
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ))^T
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} ) ig] \ &\qquad - 2	ilde f(	au)	ilde\Lambda(	au)	ilde\Lambda(s)\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s))} ig[(
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ))^T
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} ) ig]\ &\overset{\eqref{eq: score_process_corss_term_dt}}{=} 	ilde\Lambda^2(	au)\cdot  rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}	au}\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)} ig[\|
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) ||^2 + 2	ilde f(	au)	ilde\Lambda^2(	au)\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)} ig[\|
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) ||^2. \end{align*} It follows that  egin{equation}  egin{split} &  rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}	au}\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)} ig[\|
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) ||^2 + 2	ilde f(	au)\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)} ig[\|
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) ||^2\ &= 	ilde g^2(	au)\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)} ig[\|
abla^2\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c})\|^2_F ig]. \end{split} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Ito isometry gives the Frobenius-norm characterization

nodes.name: Differential inequality via Young's inequality
nodes.statement:
For any fixed $s > 0$ and $	au > s$, \eqref{eq: score_process_corss_term_dt} and \eqref{eq: F_norm_characterization} lead to  egin{align*} & rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}	au}\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s))}  ig[\|
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) - 
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} )\|^2 ig]\ &=  rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}	au}\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)} ig[\|
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} )\|^2 ig] - 2 rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}	au}\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s))} ig[(
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ))^T
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} ) ig]\ &= 	ilde g^2(	au)\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)} ig[\|
abla^2\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c})\|^2_F ig] - 2	ilde f(	au)\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)} ig[\|
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) ||^2\ &\qquad + 2\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s))} ig[	ilde f(	au)(
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} ))^T
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c})  ig]\ &= 	ilde g^2(	au)\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)} ig[\|
abla^2\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c})\|^2_F ig] \ &\qquad - 2	ilde f(	au)\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s))} ig[\|
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) - 
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} )||^2 ig]\ &\qquad + 2	ilde f(	au)\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s))}  ig[(
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} ) - 
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ))^T
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} ) ig]. \end{align*} However, by Young's inequality,  egin{align*} &\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s))} ig[(
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) - 
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} ))^T
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} ) ig]\ &\le  rac{1}{2} igg[\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s))} ig[\|
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) - 
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} )\|^2 ig] + \mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s)} ig[\|
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} )\|^2 ig] igg]. \end{align*} Therefore, we have  egin{align*} & rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}	au}\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s))}  ig[\|
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) - 
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} )\|^2 ig]\ &\le 	ilde f(	au)\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s)} ig[\|
abla\log q_{T_g - s}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(s) | \mathbf{c} )\|^2 ig] + 	ilde g^2(	au)\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au)} ig[\|
abla^2\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c})\|^2_F ig]. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Differential inequality via Young's inequality

nodes.name: Integrate using Lemmas 9 and 11
nodes.statement:
Let $s=	au_k$ and $	au\in[	au_k, 	au_{k + 1}]$. Integrate both sides of the above equation from $	au_k$ to $	au$ and use Lemma ef{lemma: score_function_norm_bound} and Lemma ef{lemma: hessian_score_bound} to obtain  egin{align*} &\mathbb{E}_{(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au), 	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au_k))} ig[\|
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au) | \mathbf{c} ) - 
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au_k}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au_k) | \mathbf{c} )\|^2 ig]\ &\le \int_{	au_k}^{	au}	ilde f(u)\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au_k)} ig[\|
abla\log q_{T_g - 	au_k}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(	au_k) | \mathbf{c} )\|^2 ig] + 	ilde g^2(u)\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(u)} ig[\|
abla^2\log q_{T_g - u}(	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(u) | \mathbf{c})\|^2_F ig]\mathrm{d} u\ &\le \int_{	au_k}^{	au}	ilde f(u)d\sigma^{-2}_{T_g - 	au_k} + 	ilde g^2(u)d\sigma^{-4}_{T_g - u} -  rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} r} ig(\sigma_{T - r}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{	ilde{\mathbf{Y}}(r)\sim q_{T_g - r}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{T_g - r})] ig) ig|_{r=u} \mathrm{d} u\ &\le \int_{	au_k}^{	au}	ilde f(u)d\sigma^{-2}_{T_g - 	au_k} + 	ilde g^2(u)d\sigma^{-4}_{T_g - u} \mathrm{d} u \ &\qquad + \sigma_{T - 	au_k}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(T_g - 	au_k)}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{T_g - 	au_k})] - \sigma_{T - 	au}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(T_g - 	au)}[	ext{trace}( oldsymbol{\Sigma}_{T_g - 	au})], \end{align*} where we omit to write out the dependency of $ oldsymbol{\Sigma}_	au$ on $\mathbf{Y}(	au)$ and $\mathbf{c}$ for simplicity.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate using Lemmas 9 and 11

nodes.name: Translate to the forward process
nodes.statement: Finally, for the forward process $\mathbf{Y}$ in \eqref{eq: forward_SDE_DDPM}, since $\tilde{\mathbf{Y}}(\tau) = \mathbf{Y}(T_g - \tau)$ for any $\tau\in[0, T_g]$, we have for $\tau >0$ and $\tau\in[\tau_{k - 1}, \tau_k]$, \begin{align*} &\mathbb{E}_{(\mathbf{Y}(\tau), \mathbf{Y}(\tau_k))}\big[\|\nabla\log q_{\tau}(\mathbf{Y}(\tau) | \mathbf{c}) - \nabla\log q_{\tau_k}(\mathbf{Y}(\tau_k) | \mathbf{c} ) \|^2\big]\\ &\le \int_{\tau}^{\tau_k} f(s)d\sigma^{-2}_{\tau_k} + g^2(s)d\sigma^{-4}_{s} \mathrm{d} s + \big(\sigma_{\tau_k}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau_k)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\tau_k})] - \sigma_{\tau}^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\tau})]\big). \end{align*} This completes our proof.
nodes.statement_short: Translate to the forward process

nodes.name: Bound per condition using score norm bounds
nodes.statement: For a given condition $\mathbf{c}$, recall the definition of $\tau_{lipz}(\mathbf{c}), k_0(\mathbf{c})$ and $k_1$ in the proof of Lemma \ref{lemma: score_discretization_error_bound} in Appendix \ref{sec: score_discretization_error}. By Lemma 14 and Lemma 21 of \cite{chen2023improved} and our Lemma \ref{lemma: score_function_norm_bound}, we can derive \begin{align*} &\sum_{k=1}^{K}\int_{\tau_{k - 1}}^{\tau_{k}}[g^2(\tau_k) - g^2(\tau)]^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_{\tau}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})} \big[\big\|\nabla\log q_\tau(\mathbf{Y}(\tau) | \mathbf{c})\big\|^2\big] \mathrm{d}\tau\\ &\lesssim \sum_{k=1}^{K}\int_{\tau_{k - 1}}^{\tau_{k}}(\Delta\tau)^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_{\tau}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})} \big[\big\|\nabla\log q_\tau(\mathbf{Y}(\tau) | \mathbf{c})\big\|^2\big] \mathrm{d}\tau\\ &\lesssim \sum_{k=1}^{k_0(\mathbf{c}) - 1} \bigg[\int_{\tau_{k - 1}}^{\tau_{k}}(\Delta\tau)^2\cdot dL(\mathbf{c})\lambda_\tau^{-1} \mathrm{d}\tau \bigg] + \int_{\tau_{k_0(\mathbf{c}) - 1}}^{\tau_{lipz}(\mathbf{c})}(\Delta\tau)^2\cdot dL(\mathbf{c})\lambda_\tau^{-1} \mathrm{d}\tau \\ &\qquad + \int_{\tau_{lipz}(\mathbf{c})}^{\tau_{k_0(\mathbf{c})}}(\Delta\tau)^2\cdot d\sigma^{-2}_\tau \mathrm{d}\tau + \sum_{k_0(\mathbf{c}) + 1}^K\bigg[\int_{\tau_{k - 1}}^{\tau_{k}}(\Delta\tau)^2\cdot d\sigma^{-2}_\tau \mathrm{d}\tau\bigg]\\ &\overset{\eqref{eq: expoenetial_approximation} }{\lesssim} \int_{0}^{\tau_{lipz}(\mathbf{c})} d(\Delta\tau)^2L(\mathbf{c})(1 + a\tau^2/4 + b\tau/2) \mathrm{d}\tau + \int_{\tau_{lipz}(\mathbf{c})}^{\tau_{k_1}} \frac{d(\Delta\tau)^2}{a\tau^2/2 + b\tau} \mathrm{d}\tau + \int_{\tau_{k_1}}^{T_g} d(\Delta\tau)^2 \mathrm{d}\tau\\ &\lesssim d(\Delta\tau)^2L(\mathbf{c})\cdot \tau_{lipz}(\mathbf{c}) + d(\Delta\tau)^2\int_{\tau_{lipz}(\mathbf{c})}^{\tau_{k_1}}\bigg(\frac{1}{\tau} + \frac{1}{\tau^2} \bigg)\mathrm{d}\tau + d(\Delta\tau)^2T_g\\ &\overset{\eqref{eq: lipz_index_approximation}}{\lesssim} d(\Delta\tau)^2\bigg(L(\mathbf{c}) + 2L_2(\mathbf{c}) + 1/2 + \ln\big(2L_2(\mathbf{c}) + 1/2\big) + T_g \bigg)\\ &\overset{\eqref{eq: lipschitz_constant}}{\lesssim} d(\Delta\tau)^2\bigg(L(\mathbf{c}) + T_g + 1 \bigg). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound per condition using score norm bounds

nodes.name: Average over conditions
nodes.statement: Taking expectation on both sides w.r.t. $\mathbf{c}\sim\mathbf{C}$, we obtain \begin{align*} &\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{c}\sim\mathbf{C}}\bigg[\sum_{k=1}^{K}\int_{\tau_{k - 1}}^{\tau_{k}}[g^2(\tau_k) - g^2(\tau)]^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_{\tau}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})} \big[\big\|\nabla\log q_\tau(\mathbf{Y}(\tau) | \mathbf{c})\big\|^2\big] \mathrm{d}\tau\bigg]\\ &\lesssim d(\Delta\tau)^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{c}\sim\mathbf{C}}\bigg[L(\mathbf{c}) + T_g + 1\bigg]\\ &\lesssim d(\Delta\tau)^2[L_1 + T_g + 1]. \end{align*} The proof is therefore complete.
nodes.statement_short: Average over conditions

nodes.name: Name the two drift functions
nodes.statement: Denote the following drift functions of \eqref{eq: piece_reverse_SDE} and \eqref{eq: piece_reverse_SDE_simulation} for simplicity: \begin{align*} \tilde F(\mathbf{y}, \tau) := \tilde f(\tau)\mathbf{y} + \tilde g^2(\tau) \nabla\log q_{T_g - \tau}(\mathbf{y} | \mathbf{c}),\quad \tilde F_\theta(\tilde{\mathbf{z}}):= \tilde f(\tau_k)\tilde{\mathbf{z}} + \tilde g^2(\tau_k) s_\theta(T_g - \tau_k, \tilde{\mathbf{z}}, \mathbf{c}). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Name the two drift functions

nodes.name: Proof of part (a)
nodes.statement_short: Proof of part (a)

nodes.name: Auxiliary Gaussian process
nodes.statement: We first prove Lemma \ref{lemma: KL_dt}(a). Consider an auxiliary process $\{\tilde{\mathbf{Y}}^a(\tau): \tau\in(\tau_k, \tau_{k + 1}]\}$, which also starts from $\tilde{\mathbf{Y}}^a(\tau_k) = \tilde{\mathbf{z}}$, with the dynamic \begin{align} \mathrm{d}\tilde{\mathbf{Y}}^a(\tau) &= [\tilde f(\tau_k)\tilde{\mathbf{z}} + \tilde g^2(\tau_k) \nabla\log q_{T_g - \tau_k}(\tilde {\mathbf{z}} | \mathbf{c})]\mathrm{d}\tau + \tilde g(\tau) \mathrm{d}\tilde{\mathbf{B}}(\tau):=\tilde F_a(\tilde{\mathbf{z}})\mathrm{d}\tau + \tilde g(\tau) \mathrm{d} \tilde{\mathbf{B}}(\tau). \end{align} Denote by $\tilde p_{\tau | \tau_k}^a(\cdot | \tilde{\mathbf{z}})$ the conditional density of $\tilde{\mathbf{Y}}^a(\tau)$ given $\tilde{\mathbf{Y}}^a(\tau_k) = \tilde{\mathbf{z}}$. Then, $\tilde p_{\tau | \tau_k}^a(\cdot | \tilde{\mathbf{z}})$ is a Gaussian density with mean $\tilde {\mathbf{z}} + (\tau - \tau_k)\tilde F_a(\tilde{\mathbf{z}})$ and covariance $\int_{\tau_k}^{\tau}\tilde g^2(s)\mathrm{d} s\cdot I_d$.
nodes.statement_short: Auxiliary Gaussian process

nodes.name: Split KL through the auxiliary density
nodes.statement: Note that, for any $\tau\in(\tau_k, \tau_{k + 1}]$ and $\tilde{\mathbf{z}}\in\mathbb{R}^d$, \begin{align} \text{KL}\big(\tilde p_{\tau | \tau_k}(\cdot | \tilde{\mathbf{z}}) || \tilde p^\theta_{\tau | \tau_k}(\cdot | \tilde{\mathbf{z}})\big) &= \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \tilde p_{\tau | \tau_k}(\mathbf{y} | \tilde{\mathbf{z}}) \log\frac{\tilde p_{\tau | \tau_k}(\mathbf{y} | \tilde{\mathbf{z}})}{\tilde p_{\tau | \tau_k}^\theta(\mathbf{y} | \tilde{\mathbf{z}})}\mathrm{d}\mathbf{y}\nonumber\\ &= \text{KL}\big(\tilde p_{\tau | \tau_k}(\cdot | \tilde{\mathbf{z}}) || \tilde p_{\tau | \tau_k}^a(\cdot | \tilde{\mathbf{z}})\big) + \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \tilde p_{\tau | \tau_k}(\mathbf{y} | \tilde{\mathbf{z}}) \log\frac{\tilde p_{\tau | \tau_k}^a(\mathbf{y} | \tilde{\mathbf{z}})}{\tilde p^\theta_{\tau | \tau_k}(\mathbf{y} | \tilde{\mathbf{z}})}\mathrm{d}\mathbf{y}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Split KL through the auxiliary density

nodes.name: First KL term vanishes in the limit
nodes.statement: Using a similar argument as in the proof of Lemma 7(2) in \cite{chen2023improved}, we can obtain that, for almost every $\tilde{\mathbf{z}}\in\mathbb{R}^d$, \begin{align*} \lim_{\tau\to\tau_k+}\text{KL}(\tilde p_{\tau | \tau_k}(\cdot | \tilde{\mathbf{z}})|| \tilde p^a_{\tau | \tau_k}(\cdot | \tilde{\mathbf{z}})) = 0. \end{align*} It follows that \begin{align} \mathbb{E}_{\tilde{\mathbf{Y}}(\tau_k)\sim \tilde p_{\tau_k}}\bigg[\lim_{\tau\to\tau_k+}\text{KL}(\tilde p_{\tau | \tau_k}(\cdot | \tilde{\mathbf{Y}}(\tau_k))|| \tilde p^a_{\tau | \tau_k}(\cdot | \tilde{\mathbf{Y}}(\tau_k)))\bigg] = 0. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: First KL term vanishes in the limit

nodes.name: Gaussian cross term is nonpositive in the limit
nodes.statement_short: Gaussian cross term is nonpositive in the limit

nodes.name: Combine and use nonnegativity of KL
nodes.statement: Combining \eqref{eq: limit_KL_decomposion}, \eqref{eq: limit_KL_auxiliary} and \eqref{eq: limit_KL_Gaussian}, and using the non-negativity property of KL-divergence, we obtain \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}_{\tilde{\mathbf{Y}}(\tau_k)\sim\tilde p_{\tau_k}} \bigg[\lim_{\tau \to \tau_k+}\text{KL}\big(\tilde p_{\tau | \tau_k}(\cdot | \tilde{\mathbf{Y}}(\tau_k)) || \tilde p^\theta_{\tau | \tau_k}(\cdot | \tilde{\mathbf{Y}}(\tau_k))\big)\bigg]= 0, \end{align*} which proves Lemma \ref{lemma: KL_dt}(a).
nodes.statement_short: Combine and use nonnegativity of KL

nodes.name: Proof of part (b)
nodes.statement:
Next, we consider bounding $ rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}	au}	ext{KL}(	ilde p_{	au | 	au_k}(\cdot | 	ilde{\mathbf{z}})|| 	ilde p^	heta_{	au | 	au_k}(\cdot | 	ilde{\mathbf{z}})$ for Lemma ef{lemma: KL_dt}(b). For any given $	ilde{\mathbf{z}}\in\mathbb{R}^d$, we use the following notations for simplicity,  egin{align*}  ar p_	au:= 	ilde p_{	au | 	au_k}(\cdot | 	ilde{\mathbf{z}}), \quad  ar p^	heta_	au:= 	ilde p^	heta_{	au | 	au_k}(\cdot | 	ilde{\mathbf{z}}). \end{align*} Using the same argument as in the proof of Lemma 6 in \cite{chen2023improved}, we have  egin{align}  rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}	au}	ext{KL}( ar p_	au ||  ar p^	heta_	au) = \int_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^d} \log  rac{ ar p_	au}{ ar p_	au^	heta}\cdot  rac{\partial  ar p_	au}{\partial	au}(\mathbf{y})\mathrm{d} \mathbf{y} - \int_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^d}  rac{ ar p_	au}{ ar p_	au^	heta}\cdot  rac{\partial  ar p^	heta_	au}{\partial	au}(\mathbf{y})\mathrm{d} \mathbf{y}. \end{align} Applying the Fokker-Planck equation to \eqref{eq: piece_reverse_SDE} and \eqref{eq: piece_reverse_SDE_simulation}, we get the evolutions of $ ar p_	au$ and $ ar p^	heta_	au$ as  egin{align*}  rac{\partial  ar p_	au}{\partial	au}(\mathbf{y}) &=

abla  ar p_	au(\mathbf{y}) igg],\  rac{\partial  ar p^	heta_	au}{\partial	au}(\mathbf{y}) &=

abla  ar p^	heta_	au(\mathbf{y}) igg]. \end{align*} It again follows from the Fokker-Planck equation that the first term of \eqref{eq: density_KL_dt} can be expressed as  egin{align*} \int_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^d} \log  rac{ ar p_	au}{ ar p_	au^	heta}\cdot  rac{\partial  ar p_	au}{\partial	au}(\mathbf{y})\mathrm{d} \mathbf{y} &= \int_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^d}  ar p_	au(\mathbf{y}) [	ilde F(\mathbf{y}, 	au)]^T
abla\log rac{ ar p_	au}{ ar p_	au^	heta}(\mathbf{y})\mathrm{d} \mathbf{y} -  rac{	ilde g^2(	au)}{2}\int_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^d} [
abla ar p_	au(\mathbf{y})]^T
abla\log rac{ ar p_	au}{ ar p_	au^	heta}(\mathbf{y}) \mathrm{d} \mathbf{y}, \end{align*} and the second term of \eqref{eq: density_KL_dt} as  egin{align*} \int_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^d}  rac{ ar p_	au}{ ar p_	au^	heta}\cdot  rac{\partial  ar p^	heta_	au}{\partial	au}(\mathbf{y})\mathrm{d} \mathbf{y} = \int_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^d}  ar p^	heta_	au(\mathbf{y}) [	ilde F_	heta(	ilde{\mathbf{z}})]^T 
abla rac{ ar p_	au}{ ar p_	au^	heta}(\mathbf{y}) \mathrm{d} \mathbf{y} -  rac{	ilde g^2(	au_k)}{2}\int_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^d} [
abla ar p^	heta_	au(\mathbf{y})]^T
abla rac{ ar p_	au}{ ar p_	au^	heta}(\mathbf{y})\mathrm{d} \mathbf{y}. \end{align*} We compute  egin{align} &\int_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^d}  ar p_	au(\mathbf{y}) [	ilde F(\mathbf{y}, 	au)]^T
abla\log rac{ ar p_	au}{ ar p_	au^	heta}(\mathbf{y})\mathrm{d} \mathbf{y} - \int_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^d}  ar p^	heta_	au(\mathbf{y}) 	ilde F_	heta(	ilde{\mathbf{z}})^T
abla rac{ ar p_	au}{ ar p_	au^	heta}(\mathbf{y}) \mathrm{d} \mathbf{y} 
onumber\ &= \int_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^d}  ar p_	au(\mathbf{y}) [	ilde F(\mathbf{y}, 	au)]^T
abla\log rac{ ar p_	au}{ ar p_	au^	heta}(\mathbf{y})\mathrm{d} \mathbf{y} - \int_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^d}  ar p_	au(\mathbf{y}) 	ilde F_	heta(	ilde{\mathbf{z}})^T
abla\log rac{ ar p_	au}{ ar p_	au^	heta}(\mathbf{y}) \mathrm{d} \mathbf{y}
onumber\ &= \int_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^d}  ar p_	au(\mathbf{y}) [	ilde F(\mathbf{y}, 	au) - 	ilde F_	heta(	ilde{\mathbf{z}})]^T

In addition, we have  egin{align} & rac{	ilde g^2(	au_k)}{2}\int_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^d} [
abla ar p^	heta_	au(\mathbf{y})]^T

onumber\ &=  rac{	ilde g^2(	au_k)}{2}\int_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^d} ar p_	au(\mathbf{y})[
abla\log ar p^	heta_	au(\mathbf{y})]^T
abla\log rac{ ar p_	au}{ ar p_	au^	heta}(\mathbf{y})\mathrm{d} \mathbf{y} -  rac{	ilde g^2(	au)}{2}\int_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^d}  ar p_	au(\mathbf{y})[
abla\log ar p_	au(\mathbf{y})]^T
abla\log rac{ ar p_	au}{ ar p_	au^	heta}(\mathbf{y}) \mathrm{d} \mathbf{y}
onumber\ &= - rac{1}{2}\int_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^d}  ar p_	au(\mathbf{y})[	ilde g^2(	au)
abla\log ar p_	au(\mathbf{y}) - 	ilde g^2(	au_k)
abla\log ar p^	heta_	au(\mathbf{y})]^T 
abla\log rac{ ar p_	au}{ ar p_	au^	heta}(\mathbf{y})\mathrm{d} \mathbf{y}
onumber\ &=  rac{1}{2}\int_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^d}  ar p_	au(\mathbf{y})[	ilde g^2(	au_k) - 	ilde g^2(	au)][
abla\log ar p_	au(\mathbf{y})]^T

nodes.name: Hessian via posterior covariance
nodes.statement: Recall that $\mathbf{Y}(\tau) | \mathbf{Y}(0)\sim\mathcal{N}(\lambda_\tau\mathbf{Y}(0), \sigma_\tau^2I_d)$. Using a similar argument as in the proof of Lemma 5 of \cite{bentonnearly}, we obtain \begin{align*} \nabla^2\log q_\tau(\mathbf{y}_\tau|\mathbf{c}) = -\sigma_\tau^{-2}I_d + \sigma_\tau^{-4}{\text{Cov}}_{q_{0|\tau}(\cdot | \mathbf{y}(\tau), \mathbf{c})}\big(\mathbf{y}(\tau) - \lambda_\tau\mathbf{Y}(0)\big) = -\sigma_\tau^{-2}I_d + \sigma_\tau^{-4}\lambda_\tau^2\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Compute Frobenius norm and apply (61)
nodes.statement: Noting that $\|A\|_F^2 = \text{trace}(A^TA)$ for a matrix $A$ and that $1 > \lambda_\tau^2 = \exp(-a\tau^2/2 - b\tau) = 2\sigma_\tau\dot\sigma_\tau/(a\tau + b)$, we can directly compute \begin{align*} &\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_\tau(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}\big[\|\nabla^2\log q_\tau(\mathbf{Y}_\tau|\mathbf{c})\|_F^2\big] \\ &= d\sigma_\tau^{-4} - 2\sigma_\tau^{-6}\lambda_\tau^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau)] + \sigma_\tau^{-8}\lambda_\tau^4\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau^2)]\\ &\le d\sigma_\tau^{-4} - 2\sigma_\tau^{-6}\lambda_\tau^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau)] + \sigma_\tau^{-8}\lambda_\tau^2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau^2)]\\ &\overset{\eqref{eq: posterior_cov_trace_dt}}{=} d\sigma_\tau^{-4} - \frac{4\sigma_\tau^{-5}\dot\sigma_\tau}{a\tau + b}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau)] + \frac{2\sigma_\tau^{-7}\dot\sigma_\tau}{a\tau + b}\cdot \frac{\sigma_\tau^3}{2\dot\sigma_\tau}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\tau}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau)]\\ &= d\sigma_\tau^{-4} - \frac{4\sigma_\tau^{-5}\dot\sigma_\tau}{a\tau + b}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau)] + \frac{\sigma_\tau^{-4}}{a\tau + b}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\tau}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau))}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau)]\\ &= d\sigma_\tau^{-4} + \frac{1}{a\tau + b}\cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\tau}\bigg(\sigma_\tau^{-4}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\sim q_\tau(\cdot | \mathbf{c})}[\text{trace}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_\tau)]\bigg). \end{align*} The proof is complete by virtue of $g^2(\tau) = a\tau + b$.

nodes.name: Ito's formula for $\Lambda Y$
nodes.statement: Letting $\Lambda(\tau) = \exp\big(\int_{0}^\tau f(s)\mathrm{d} s\big)$ and applying It\^{o}'s formula to the forward SDE \eqref{eq: forward_SDE_DDPM} under the condition $\mathbf{c}$, we have \begin{align*} \mathrm{d} [\Lambda(\tau)\mathbf{Y}(\tau)] = f(\tau)\Lambda(\tau)\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau + \Lambda(\tau)\big[-f(\tau)\mathbf{Y}(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau + g(\tau)\mathrm{d} \mathbf{B}(\tau)\big] = \Lambda(\tau)g(\tau)\mathrm{d} \mathbf{B}(\tau). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Ito's formula for $\Lambda Y$
nodes.section: C.2 Proof of Lemma 11 via Stochastic Localization

nodes.name: Dambis-Dubins-Schwarz time change
nodes.statement: By the Dambis-Dubins–Schwarz theorem {\citep[Theorem 3.4.6]{karatzas2014brownian}}, there is a process $(\hat{\mathbf{B}}(s))_{s\ge 0}$ such that under the time change \begin{align*} \kappa(s) := \inf\bigg\{\tau: \int_{0}^\tau\Lambda^2(u)g^2(u)\mathrm{d} u > s\bigg\} = \inf\bigg\{\tau: \exp\big(a\tau^2/2 + b\tau\big) - 1> s\bigg\}, \end{align*} we have \begin{align*} \hat{\mathbf{B}}(e^{a\tau^2/2 + b\tau} - 1) = \int_{0}^\tau\Lambda(u)g(u)\mathrm{d} \mathbf{B}(u), \end{align*} where $(\hat{\mathbf{B}}(s))_{s\ge 0}$ is a standard Brownian motion w.r.t. the filtration $\big(\mathcal{F}_{\kappa(s)}\big)_{s\ge0}$, while $(\mathcal{F}_\tau)_{\tau \ge 0}$ is the natural filtration generated by $(\mathbf{B}(\tau))_{\tau \ge 0}$. Then, for any $s > 0$, we have \begin{align*} \Lambda(\kappa(s))\mathbf{Y}(\kappa(s)) = \mathbf{Y}(0) + \int_{0}^{\kappa(s)}\Lambda(u)g(u)\mathrm{d} \mathbf{B}(u) = \mathbf{Y}(0) + \hat{\mathbf{B}}(s). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Dambis-Dubins-Schwarz time change
nodes.section: C.2 Proof of Lemma 11 via Stochastic Localization

nodes.name: Identify the stochastic localization
nodes.statement: Now, if we set $\mathbf{U}(0) = 0$ and \begin{align*} \mathbf{U}(s) := s\Lambda(\kappa(s^{-1}))\mathbf{Y}(\kappa(s^{-1})) = s\mathbf{Y}(0) + s\hat{\mathbf{B}}(s^{-1}),\ \text{for } s > 0, \end{align*} then we find that $\mathbf{U}$ satisfies the definition of the stochastic localization in \eqref{eq: stochastic_localization}, because $\mathbf{Y}(0)\sim p_{\text{target}}(\cdot | \mathbf{c})$ and the law of $\big(s\hat{\mathbf{B}}(s^{-1})\big)_{s\ge 0}$ is the same as the law of $\big(\hat{\mathbf{B}}(s)\big)_{s\ge 0}$. The proof is complete by noting that $\kappa(s^{-1}) = \tau(s)$ in \eqref{eq: diffusion_localization_time_change} and $\Lambda(\tau) = \lambda_\tau^{-1}$ in \eqref{eq: forward_SDE_coeff}.
nodes.statement_short: Identify the stochastic localization

nodes.name: Loop over episodes
nodes.statement: \FOR{episode $m = 1$ \TO $M$} \STATE Generate $H_s$ synthetic asset price paths by $G(\theta)$. \STATE Initialize $n = 0$ and store $x^{(j)}(t_n) \leftarrow x(0)$ for $j=1,..., H + H_s$. \WHILE{$n < N_T$} \FOR{path $j=1$ \TO $H + H_s$} \STATE{Generate action $a^{(j)}(t_n)\sim \pi_{\psi}(\cdot|t_n, x^{(j)}(t_n); w)$. Compute and store the test functions \vspace{-3mm} \[ \xi^{(j)}(t_n)= \frac{\partial J_\varphi}{\partial \varphi}(t_{n},x^{(j)}(t_n); w),\quad \zeta^{(j)}(t_n) = \frac{\partial q_{\psi}}{\partial \psi}(t_{n}, x^{(j)}(t_n), a^{(j)}(t_n); w). \] \vspace{-5mm} \IF{$j \le H$} \STATE In the real wealth simulator: $x^{(j)}(t_{n + 1}) = Wealth_{\Delta t}(t_n, x^{(j)}(t_n), a^{(j)}(t_n)).$ \ELSE \STATE In the synthetic wealth simulator: $x^{(j)}(t_{n + 1}) = Wealth_{\Delta t}(t_n, x^{(j)}(t_n), a^{(j)}(t_n); G(\theta)).$ \ENDIF } \ENDFOR \STATE Update $n \leftarrow n + 1$. \ENDWHILE \STATE Store the terminal wealth $x^{(j)}(T; m) \leftarrow x^{(j)}(t_{N_T})$ for $j=1,..., H + H_s$. \STATE For path $j=1, \cdots H + H_s$, compute \vspace{-3mm} \begin{align*} \Delta \varphi^{(j)} = \sum_{n=0}^{N_T - 1} \xi^{(j)}(t_n) \big[ J_\varphi(t_{n + 1}, x^{(j)}(t_{n + 1}); w) - J_\varphi(t_n, x^{(j)}(t_n); w) -q_{\psi}(t_n, x^{(j)}(t_n) ,a^{(j)}(t_n); w)\Delta t \big],\\ \Delta \psi^{(j)} = \sum_{n=0}^{N_T - 1} \zeta^{(j)}(t_n)\big[ J_\varphi(t_{n + 1}, x^{(j)}(t_{n + 1}); w) - J_\varphi(t_n, x^{(j)}(t_n); w) - q_{\psi}(t_n, x^{(j)}(t_n), a^{(j)}(t_n); w)\Delta t \big] . \end{align*} \vspace{-3mm} \STATE Update $\varphi$ and $\psi$: $\varphi \leftarrow \varphi + \frac{\alpha_{\varphi}(m)}{H + H_s}\sum_{j=1}^{H + H_s}\Delta \varphi^{(j)},\ \psi \leftarrow \psi + \cdot\frac{\alpha_{\psi}(m)}{H + H_s} \sum_{j=1}^{H + H_s}\Delta \psi ^{(j)}$ \vspace{1mm} \STATE Update $w$ (Lagrange multiplier) every $L$ episodes: \IF{$m\equiv 0$ mod $L$} \STATE{$w\leftarrow w - \alpha_w \frac{1}{L}\sum_{i=m - L + 1}^m \frac{1}{H + H_s}\sum_{j=1}^{H + H_s}x^{(j)}(T; i)$} \ENDIF
